definition_zh: 幼稚无经验的；年轻无阅历的；（鸟）羽翼未丰的
definition_en: inexperienced and immature; also (of a young bird) without feathers
core_image: 一只刚破壳、绒毛未干的雏鸟张着嘴等食：什么都还没长成
scene: 初出校门的实习生第一次主持会议，紧张得连幻灯片都翻错了页。 The callow intern assumed the deal would close in a week.
sceneCN: 这里 callow 是「幼稚无经验的」（第 2 个义项：缺乏阅历、想事简单）；句意是这位稚嫩的实习生以为一周内就能谈成这笔交易。

pos.zh: 幼稚无经验的；不成熟的

collocations.zh: 没见过世面的年轻男子

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「稚嫩；不成熟」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「稚嫩地；不老练地」（罕用）

senses.title: Without feathers, of a young bird
senses.definition: describing a newly hatched bird that has not yet grown feathers
senses.definitionCN: 形容刚孵出、还没长出羽毛的雏鸟
senses.example: The callow nestlings waited with open beaks.
senses.exampleCN: 羽翼未丰的雏鸟张着嘴等食。
senses.why: The Old English source calu meant bald, so the literal image is bare, unfinished skin.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词源 calu 意为「光秃的」，字面意象就是裸露未长成的皮肉。

senses.title: Inexperienced and immature
senses.titleCN: 幼稚无经验的；不成熟的
senses.definition: lacking the experience, judgment, or polish that comes with age and practice
senses.definitionCN: 缺少年龄和实践带来的经验、判断力与老练
senses.example: He was too callow to negotiate with the veterans.
senses.exampleCN: 他太稚嫩了，没法和这些老手谈判。
senses.why: Just as a featherless bird cannot fly, an untested person cannot handle adult demands.
senses.whyCN: 正如没有羽毛的鸟飞不起来，未经世事的人也应付不了成人的事务。

senses.title: Young in a slightly dismissive way
senses.definition: young in a way the speaker finds naive or not worth taking seriously
senses.definitionCN: 年纪轻得让说话者觉得天真可笑、不足为惧
senses.example: Some callow junior dared to question the professor.
senses.exampleCN: 某个乳臭未干的小字辈竟敢质疑教授。
senses.why: Naming immaturity is a way of ranking: the featherless image doubles as an insult about status.
senses.whyCN: 点出「未长成」本身就是在排座次：光秃秃的意象同时暗含地位低微的贬义。

senses.title: Naive in outlook or style
senses.definition: showing naïveté in judgment, writing, or art that has not yet matured
senses.definitionCN: 判断、文章或艺术创作显出未经打磨的天真与稚拙
senses.example: His first novel is callow but full of promise.
senses.exampleCN: 他的第一部长篇小说稚拙，却充满潜力。
senses.why: What is literally unfinished shows the rough surface of an unformed skill.
senses.whyCN: 「未长成」的字面义投射到未打磨的技艺上，露出粗糙的表面。

intro.en: Callow descends from Old English calu, bald, from a Proto-Germanic root for bare skin; it moved from featherless birds to untested people.
intro.cn: callow 源自古英语 calu（光秃的），出自日耳曼语族一个表「裸露」的词根，再从「无毛的雏鸟」转指「未经磨砺的人」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *gel- / *kal- is associated with cold and bareness, the state of skin stripped of covering.
items.cn: 重构词根 *gel- / *kal- 与「寒冷、裸露」相关，指失去覆盖物的皮肤状态。

items.en: Germanic *kalwaz meant bald or bare, surviving in German kahl with the same meaning.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *kalwaz 意为光秃的、裸的，德语 kahl 至今保留同义。

items.en: Old English calu meant bald or featherless, applied to people, animals, and even bare land.
items.cn: 古英语 calu 意为秃的、无毛的，可用于人、动物乃至裸露的土地。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word had shifted from bald feathers to callow youth, immaturity in people.
items.cn: 至十六世纪，词义已从「无毛」转向 callow youth，形容人的不成熟。

items.en: Today the bird sense is rare and mainly literary; the immaturity sense dominates, often in the fixed phrase callow youth.
items.cn: 如今雏鸟义已罕见，主要见于文学；「不成熟」义占主导，常见固定搭配 callow youth。

note.en: Callow looks close to callous in sound and spelling but has a completely different root and meaning.
note.cn: callow 的音与形都和 callous 很接近，但词根与词义完全不同。

entries.definition: Emotionally hardened; indifferent to suffering; from the Latin root for hard skin.
entries.definitionCN: 冷酷无情的，对痛苦麻木；源自拉丁语「硬皮」词根，与 callow 词源不同。

entries.definition: A patch of hardened skin; also the Latin-rooted noun family of callous.
entries.definitionCN: 硬皮、老茧；属 callous 同一拉丁词族，与 callow 无关。

entries.definition: Not deep in thought or feeling; rhymes with callow but unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 思想或情感浅薄的，与 callow 押韵但词源无关。

entries.definition: Left unplanted, as of farmland; a near rhyme often confused in reading.
entries.definitionCN: （农田）休耕的，与 callow 形近音近，阅读时易混。

entries.definition: Inexperienced, as in a green recruit who has not learned the ropes.
entries.definitionCN: 没经验的，如尚未上手的「新手」green recruit。

entries.definition: Lacking worldly experience and too ready to believe others.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏世故、轻信他人的天真者。

entries.definition: Not fully developed emotionally or behaviorally.
entries.definitionCN: 情感或行为上尚未发育成熟的。

entries.definition: A noun for an inexperienced newcomer.
entries.definitionCN: 指生手的名词，义为「新手、生瓜蛋子」。

entries.definition: Made experienced and competent by long practice.
entries.definitionCN: 经长期历练而老练的，是 callow 的反义对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the bald-bird image and the fixed phrase callow youth.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「光秃雏鸟」意象与固定搭配 callow youth 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root link: Old English calu, bald, survives inside callow, literally a bald, featherless bird.
normal.cn: 词根线索：古英语 calu（光秃的）藏在 callow 里，字面就是一只光秃秃没长毛的鸟。

normal.en: Fixed phrase: callow youth is the classic collocation in classic novels and exams.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：callow youth（少不更事的年轻人）是经典小说和考试中的标配组合。

normal.en: Contrast pair: callow (no experience) versus seasoned (full of experience) are natural antonyms.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：callow（零经验）与 seasoned（老练）是一对天然反义词。

normal.en: Sound guard: callow ends in -ow like shallow and fallow; callous ends in -ous; feel the rhyme to keep them apart.
normal.cn: 音形防守：callow 以 -ow 结尾，与 shallow、fallow 同韵；callous 以 -ous 结尾，靠韵脚分开。

normal.en: The German cousin kahl, bald, shows the same root still alive in another language.
normal.cn: 德语同源词 kahl（光秃的）证明这个词根在另一门语言里仍然存活。

abstract.en: A baby bird on the nest edge, wings bare and useless, certain it can fly.
abstract.cn: 巢边的雏鸟，翅膀光秃无用，却自信满满地认定自己会飞。

abstract.en: A fresh diploma in one hand and no idea what a deadline feels like.
abstract.cn: 一只手举着崭新的毕业证，另一只手对截止日期的滋味一无所知。

abstract.en: A green shoot: upright and alive, but one frost away from learning the world.
abstract.cn: 一株嫩芽：直挺挺地活着，但一场霜冻就会让它认识世界。

examples.en: The callow recruit apologized for the mistake he did not yet know how to avoid.
examples.cn: 这个稚嫩的新兵为自己还不知道如何避免的错误道歉。

examples.en: Her callow essays from the first semester bear no resemblance to her mature later work.
examples.cn: 她第一学期稚拙的文章与后来成熟的作品判若两人。

examples.en: In the film the callow youth grows into a hardened commander.
examples.cn: 影片中乳臭未干的少年成长为意志坚硬的指挥官。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凯漏」——新人凯旋却处处露怯、漏洞百出，一看就是个没经验的雏儿；谐音联想到「凯」旋路上「漏」了怯，便是幼稚无经验的 callow。

root: 源自古英语 calu（光秃的、无毛的），出自原始日耳曼语 *kalwaz（裸的），与德语 kahl 同源；一般认为可上溯至印欧词根 *gel-（冷、裸露）。本义「光秃无毛」，十六世纪起转指人的「稚嫩无经验」。注意与拉丁词源的 callous（冷酷的）没有任何亲缘关系。

sensesIntro.en: From the literal featherless hatchling the word extends to untested people, dismissive comments about youth, and unpolished work.
sensesIntro.cn: 从字面的无毛雏鸟出发，词义延伸到未经磨砺的人、对年轻人的轻蔑评语以及未经打磨的作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hatchling with bare skin and no feathers, not yet ready for the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只皮肉裸露、羽毛未生的雏鸟，还飞不上天。

branches.en: THE NEST: the bird sense, bare-skinned and flightless.
branches.cn: 鸟巢：雏鸟义，光秃无毛、不能飞。

branches.en: THE PERSON: inexperience that age and practice have not yet cured.
branches.cn: 人：年龄和实践尚未治愈的无经验。

branches.en: THE JUDGMENT: a dismissive label pinned on the young.
branches.cn: 评判：贴在年轻人身上的轻蔑标签。

branches.en: THE WORK: early writing or art that has not found its polish.
branches.cn: 作品：尚未打磨出光泽的早期文字或艺术。

branches.en: THE ARC: the standard growth story from callow to seasoned.
branches.cn: 成长弧线：从稚嫩到老练的经典叙事。

intro.en: Callow is a single inherited Germanic word, not built from prefix and suffix, so its story is the root calu itself.
intro.cn: callow 是一个日耳曼语系世代相传的单词，并非由前后缀拼装，它的故事全在词根 calu 之中。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family here; the root is Germanic, so the Latin list stays empty and cousins come from the Germanic side.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁词族；词根属日耳曼语系，拉丁同源列表留空，同族词来自日耳曼一侧。

definition_zh: 用头（角）顶撞；烟蒂；枪托；酒桶；屁股（口语）
definition_en: to strike with the head or horns; also the end of a cigarette, the stock end of a gun, a large barrel, or (informal) the bottom
core_image: 公羊低头一顶，把对手撞出老远
scene: 山坡上两只公羊低着头冲向对方。 The young ram learned to butt his rival off the ledge.
sceneCN: 这里 butt 是「用头顶撞」（第 1 个义项：以头或角冲撞）；句意是这只小公羊学会了用头把对手顶下石台。

pos.zh: 烟蒂；枪托；酒桶；（口语）屁股

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 转名词，义为「顶撞行为」
由拉丁前缀加同源词根构成，义为「毗邻，紧靠」

senses.title: To strike with the head or horns
senses.definition: to hit someone or something with the head or horns, pushing forward
senses.definitionCN: 用头或角向前冲撞某人或某物
senses.example: Goats butt each other to decide who leads the herd.
senses.exampleCN: 山羊互相顶撞，决出谁是头羊。
senses.why: The image is a lowered head driven forward like a blow.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是低头向前一顶，像一次打击。

senses.title: The thick end of a tool or cigarette
senses.definition: the larger or thicker end of something, especially the leftover stub of a smoked cigarette or the stock end of a gun
senses.definitionCN: 器物较粗的一端，尤指抽剩的烟蒂或枪的托端
senses.example: He crushed the butt under his boot.
senses.exampleCN: 他一脚踩灭了烟蒂。
senses.why: The same word names the thick end that absorbs the blow, like the animal's head.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指承受冲撞的粗端，正如顶撞用的头部。

senses.title: A large cask for wine or water
senses.definition: a large barrel or cask, especially for wine, beer or rainwater
senses.definitionCN: 大桶，多用于盛酒、啤酒或雨水
senses.example: A rain butt stood under the cottage eaves.
senses.exampleCN: 农舍屋檐下放着一只接雨水的大桶。
senses.why: A separate old French word for a cask happened to match this form.
senses.whyCN: 这是古法语另一支「大桶」一词的巧合同形，与顶撞义并不同源。

senses.title: A person or thing that is mocked
senses.definition: a person or thing at whom mockery or criticism is directed
senses.definitionCN: 成为嘲笑或批评目标的人或事物
senses.example: The clumsy apprentice was the butt of every joke in the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 这个笨手笨脚的学徒成了作坊里所有笑话的靶子。
senses.why: The target of blows becomes the target of laughter.
senses.whyCN: 承受撞击的「靶」转为承受笑声的「靶」。

senses.title: The bottom (informal)
senses.definition: informal word for the part of the body one sits on
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指坐着的身体部位
senses.example: Get off your butt and help us move the table.
senses.exampleCN: 别闲坐着了，过来帮我们搬桌子。
senses.why: The thick-end sense slid to the rounded end of the body.
senses.whyCN: 「粗端」义滑移到身体浑圆的末端。

intro.en: Butt is really two or three words that look alike: a butting head from French boter, a cask from Old French butt, and a thick end from the same Germanic root as button.
intro.cn: butt 实为几个同形词：顶撞义出自法语 boter，大桶义出自古法语 butt，粗端义则与 button 同一日耳曼词根。

items.en: a Germanic root for 'to strike, push' gave Old French boter and English beat-adjacent forms.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根表示「击打、推撞」，进入古法语 boter，与英语 beat 相邻。

items.en: boter meant to push or strike; butt entered English in the sense of thrusting with the head.
items.cn: 古法语 boter 意为推撞；butt 进入英语时即指用头顶撞。

items.en: a separate Old French butt meant a cask, from Late Latin buttis.
items.cn: 古法语另一词 butt 指大桶，出自后期拉丁语 buttis。

items.en: the thick-end sense grew through archery butts and the end of a tool, later the cigarette butt.
items.cn: 十四至十六世纪，「粗端」义经射箭靶座、工具末端发展，后指烟蒂。

items.en: informal use for the bottom is American, and butt in is the common idiom for interrupting.
items.cn: 现代英语中，「屁股」义为美式口语，butt in 则是「插嘴」的常用习语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects same-form words of different origins; the near-meaning group gives striking and stub words.
note.cn: 形近组收集同形异源词；近义组是冲撞与「剩余短端」词汇。

definition_en: a person who designs the steps and movements of a dance or a staged scene
core_image: 排练厅里一个人用手比划队形
scene: 编舞者在排练厅里一遍遍调整队形。 The choreographer reshaped the lines again in the rehearsal room.

senses.title: The dance designer
senses.definition: a person who creates the steps and patterns of a dance

definition_zh: 使分心；使转向；使不安；引开
definition_en: to draw someone's attention away from what they are doing or thinking
core_image: 一个人正低头系鞋带，一只手从旁边伸来把线头轻轻一扯，结散了；那只手没有碰人，只碰了那根线。
scene: 他正低头把鞋带系成一个结，旁边有人轻轻一扯线头，结散了，低头的人还在原地，手上的活却已经断了。 A single question distracted him from the knot.
sceneCN: 这里指把注意力从正在做的事上引开（第 1 个义项：使分心）；句意为一个问题就让他的注意力离开了那个结。

pos.zh: 使分心；使转向；使不安；引开（注意力）

derivatives.zh: 分心；使人分心之物（在动词后加拉丁动作名词词尾，由动作转指该行为或造成该行为之物）
心不在焉的（加表被动的分词词尾，由「被引开」转指「心神已散」）
使人分心的（加表主动的分词词尾，由「引开」转指「正在引走注意」）
易分心的（加表「易于」的形容词词尾，由「被引开」转指「容易被引走」）

senses.title: Draw attention away
senses.definition: to make someone stop attending to one thing and attend to another
senses.definitionCN: 使某人停止留意一事而转向另一事
senses.example: A single question distracted him from the knot.
senses.exampleCN: 一个问题就让他的注意力离开了那个结。
senses.why: The prefix of apartness plus a verb of pulling gives the core: heed is pulled off its object.
senses.whyCN: 动词把某人的留意从一处挪到另一处，这一挪的核心就是「拉开」。

senses.title: Sidetrack someone from a purpose
senses.definition: to turn a person away from the aim they were pursuing, often delaying them
senses.definitionCN: 把某人从正在追求的目标上引开，常致其延误
senses.example: The dispute distracted the committee from the budget for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争执让委员会一个月没能处理预算。
senses.why: A purpose can be pulled aside as a body can: the same verb, the object changed from attention to aim.
senses.whyCN: 把留意引离目标，就是把人从路上引开，因此常带延误的后果。

senses.title: Amuse a person
senses.definition: to occupy someone pleasantly so that a worry or a wait is forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 以愉快的方式占住某人，使其忘掉忧虑或等待
senses.example: He distracted the child with a paper bird while the doctor finished.
senses.exampleCN: 医生处理完之前，他用一只纸鸟哄开了孩子的注意。
senses.why: The pleasant sense keeps the structure and drops the harm: heed is moved, but nothing is lost.
senses.whyCN: 让人愉快地分神，等于用别的东西占住他的心思，仍是同一种拉扯。

senses.title: Unsettle the mind
senses.definition: to disturb someone's composure so that thought becomes difficult
senses.definitionCN: 扰乱某人的镇定，使思考变得困难
senses.example: The letter distracted her for the rest of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让她一整天都心神不宁。
senses.why: Here what is pulled away is not attention but composure, the object being the person's whole state.
senses.whyCN: 心神被扰乱也是被拉开，只是被扯开的是镇定而非留意。

senses.title: Tear apart
senses.definition: the archaic literal sense of pulling something into pieces or in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 把某物拉成碎片或朝不同方向拉开的古老字面义
senses.example: In the older legal language, to distract a thing meant to divide it by force.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的法律用语里，「拉开」某物指以强力把它分开。
senses.why: The literal sense is the root of the family: every later meaning keeps the image of two opposed pulls.
senses.whyCN: 古义仍是物理的：把物体拉成碎片，或拉向不同方向。

senses.title: Draw off an enemy
senses.definition: to cause an opponent's force to move away from the real point of action
senses.definitionCN: 使对方力量离开真正的行动要点
senses.example: Two companies distracted the garrison while the bridge was taken.
senses.exampleCN: 两个连引开守军，同时桥被拿下。
senses.why: Military use keeps the literal pull: a force is drawn off the point it should hold.
senses.whyCN: 军事用法保留字面的拉：一支部队被从应守之处拉开。

senses.title: Draw a defender away
senses.definition: in sport, to pull a marker out of position so that space opens elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 体育中指把盯防者引离位置，从而在别处露出空当
senses.example: The winger distracted the full-back and the centre ran through.
senses.exampleCN: 边锋引开边后卫，中锋从中间穿了过去。
senses.why: Sport borrows the military pattern in miniature: a pull that creates room rather than a fight.
senses.whyCN: 体育里被拉开的是盯防位置，空当因此出现在别处。

senses.title: Split one's own focus
senses.definition: to divide one's own heed deliberately between two things, usually to the loss of both
senses.definitionCN: 有意把自己的留意分给两处，通常两处都受损
senses.example: He distracted himself with the radio and missed the turn.
senses.exampleCN: 他用收音机分了自己的心，结果错过了转弯。
senses.why: The verb can take the self as both actor and object, which shows how easily the pull becomes internal.
senses.whyCN: 把自己分成两处，仍是拉开，只是施动者与受动者同为一人。

intro.en: Distract comes from Latin distractus, the participle of distrahere 'to pull apart', built on dis- 'apart' plus trahere 'to draw, drag'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: distract 出自拉丁 distractus，即 distrahere「拉开」的分词，由表「分开」的前缀加 trahere「拉、拖」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, drag, pull'. Its deeper origin is not established; any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖、拽」。其更深来源未得到证明；凡为其提出的更早词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus trahere gave distrahere 'to pull apart, draw off in different directions'.
items.cn: 表「分开」的前缀加 trahere 构成 distrahere「拉开、朝不同方向引开」。

items.en: The participle distractus described what had been pulled apart, and English took the verb form from it.
items.cn: 分词 distractus 描述已被拉开之物，英语由此取得动词形式。

items.en: Distract is recorded in English in the sixteenth century, first for pulling the mind away and for dividing by force.
items.cn: distract 在十六世纪的英语中已有记录，最初指把心思引开，也指以强力分开。

items.en: Sport, military writing and child care each took the verb for their own kind of deliberate pulling away.
items.cn: 体育、军事写作与育儿各自取用这个动词，指自己那一类有意的引开。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed, and the pre-Latin root of trahere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：没有确切的最早书证；trahere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb of pulling apart; group two holds verbs of turning something aside.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「拉开」这一动词的词形；第二组是把某物引向别处的动词。

entries.definition: Names the pulling away or the thing that causes it; the verb names the act done to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指引开的动作或造成它的事物；动词指对人所做的那个动作。

entries.definition: An adjective for the person after the pull has worked; it is the state, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 形容被引开之后的人；是状态，而非动作。

entries.definition: An adjective for what does the pulling; it describes a thing or an event, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容做出「拉」的那一方；描述事物或事件，而非人。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb of pressing tight or hampering; it means to cause pain or hardship, not to divide attention.
entries.definitionCN: 出自一个表「压紧、阻碍」的拉丁动词；意为造成痛苦或困苦，而非分散注意。

entries.definition: To turn something aside from its course, as traffic or funds; it names the redirection but not the loss of heed.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物的路线引开，如交通或资金；指改变方向，却不含留意受损之意。

entries.definition: To move a person or a discussion onto a secondary matter; it is the second sense of distract in everyday words.
entries.definitionCN: 指把人或讨论引到次要的事情上；是 distract 第二义的日常说法。

entries.definition: To make someone uneasy or uncertain; it matches the fourth sense and says nothing about attention.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人不安或把握不定；对应第四义，且完全不说注意力。

entries.definition: To hold someone's interest pleasantly; it is the third sense of distract without the idea of a task abandoned.
entries.definitionCN: 指以愉快的方式占住某人的兴趣；是 distract 第三义去掉「任务被弃」的版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A prefix of apartness on a verb of pulling: to pull a mind off what it was holding.
normal.cn: 表「分开」的前缀加表「拉」的动词：把心从它握着东西上拉开。

normal.en: The family runs distraction, distracted, distracting and distractible, all from one verb of pulling apart.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 distraction、distracted、distracting、distractible，全出同一个表「拉开」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the directions: distract someone from work, distract attention, distract the defender.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出方向：使人从工作中分心、引开注意力、引开防守者。

normal.en: The verb can take the self as its object, which is how the pull becomes internal.
normal.cn: 这个动词可以把自己当作对象，拉扯于是变成内在的。

normal.en: The archaic sense is tearing apart, and every modern sense keeps that image of two opposed pulls.
normal.cn: 古老义是撕裂，而每个现代义都保留「两股相反的力」这一形象。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pulling one loose end of a knot while the hands stay still.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指扯住绳结的一头，而双手还停在原处。

abstract.en: Picture a paper bird held up so a child forgets the needle.

abstract.en: Picture a winger running wide so the middle opens.
abstract.cn: 想象边锋跑向边路，中路于是空出来。

examples.en: The ringing phone distracted her from the sentence she was writing.
examples.cn: 响起的电话让她从正在写的那句话上分了心。

examples.en: He distracted the child with a story while the nurse prepared the syringe.
examples.cn: 护士准备针管时，他讲了个故事哄开孩子的注意。

examples.en: The decoy force distracted the garrison long enough to cross the river.
examples.cn: 佯动部队引开守军，争取到渡河的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分开」+「拉」——把心从原处拉开：拉去别的事是分心，拉去玩是哄，拉去别处是引开。

root: 拉丁 distractus，为 distrahere「拉开」的分词 = 表「分开」的前缀 + trahere「拉、拖」；trahere 更深来源未得到证明，其更早词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: something is pulled off what it was holding. Pulled off a task it is distraction; pulled off a purpose it delays a committee; pulled off a worry it amuses a child; pulled off composure it unsettles; pulled apart in the old sense it divides by force; pulled off a position it draws off a garrison or a defender; and pulled by oneself it splits one's own focus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物从它所握的东西上拉开。从任务上拉开是分心；从目的上拉开是延误委员会；从忧虑上拉开是哄孩子；从镇定上拉开是使不安；按旧义拉开是以强力分裂；从阵位上拉开是引开守军或防守者；被自己拉开则是自拆注意力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pulling one loose end of a knot while the hands themselves stay still.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指扯住绳结的一头，而双手本身仍停在原处。

branches.en: OFF THE TASK, OFF THE AIM: heed moved to another object, and a whole committee delayed.
branches.cn: 离开任务、离开目标：留意被移到另一物，与整个委员会被延误。

branches.en: THE HARMLESS PULL: a child occupied so that a worry or a wait is forgotten.
branches.cn: 无害的拉扯：孩子的注意被占住，忧虑或等待于是被忘掉。

branches.en: THE INNER PULL: composure shaken from outside, and focus split from inside.
branches.cn: 内在的拉扯：镇定被外面撼动，与焦点被自己拆开。

branches.en: THE OLD TEARING: the literal sense of dividing a thing by force.
branches.cn: 古老的撕裂：以强力把事物分开的字面义。

branches.en: DRAWN OFF A POSITION: a garrison moved from the bridge, and a defender moved from the middle.
branches.cn: 被引离阵位：从桥边被调开的守军，与从中路被引开的防守者。

intro.en: Distract is a Latin participle used as an English verb, with a prefix of separation and a root of pulling.
intro.cn: distract 是拉丁分词用作英语动词，带表分离的前缀与表「拉」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere gives traction, tractor, extract and subtract; dis- plus trahere gives distract, distraction and distractible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trahere 衍生 traction、tractor、extract、subtract；表「分开」的前缀加 trahere 衍生 distract、distraction、distractible。

items.example: The root carries the image of force applied sideways.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「从侧面施力」的形象。

items.example: The compound added opposition to the pull.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词给「拉」加上了相反的方向。

items.example: The participle became the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成为英语动词。

items.example: Nothing distracted him from the proof.
items.exampleCN: 没有什么让他从证明上分心。

items.example: The traffic outside was a constant distraction.
items.exampleCN: 外面的车流是持续的干扰。
他心不在焉地答了一句。
发亮的屏幕很让人分心。

items.example: The class was young and distractible.
items.exampleCN: 这个班年纪小，容易分心。

definition_zh: 权力结构；一个社会、组织或群体中权力与影响力的分布方式
definition_en: the arrangement through which power and influence are distributed among people, groups and institutions
core_image: 一张楼房剖面图：顶层只有几间大办公室，越往下隔间越多，箭头一层层指向上方
scene: 会议室墙上挂着一张组织图，顶层只有三个房间，越往下隔间越多，箭头逐层指向上方。 The power structure of the university kept most decisions in the hands of a small council.
sceneCN: 这里指「一个组织中权力如何分布的总体格局」（第 1 个义项：权力分布的总格局）；句意为这所大学的权力结构把大多数决定交到一个小型理事会手中。可辨识物件：组织图、顶层办公室、隔间、箭头、会议桌。

pos.zh: 权力结构（社会或组织的权力分布，常作可数）
具体的权力层级或权力网络（可数）

collocations.phrase: the power structure of a society

forms.label: 可数复数（多种权力结构）

derivatives.zh: 基础设施（同出「建造」词根）

senses.title: Who holds power in a society
senses.titleCN: 一个社会中谁掌握权力
senses.definition: the overall distribution of authority and influence among the groups that make up a society
senses.definitionCN: 构成一个社会的各群体之间权力与影响力的总体分布
senses.example: The power structure of the university kept most decisions in the hands of a small council.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学的权力结构把大多数决定交到一个小型理事会手中。
senses.why: Power is held in patterns, not only in single hands; structure names the shape those patterns make.
senses.whyCN: 权力以格局而非单只手的方式被持有；结构一词命名的正是这些格局形成的形状。

senses.title: The formal chain of command
senses.definition: the official hierarchy that shows who reports to whom and who may decide what
senses.definitionCN: 显示谁向谁汇报、谁可以决定什么的官方层级
senses.example: The company's power structure places the board above every division.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的权力结构把董事会置于所有部门之上。
senses.why: An organization draws its power as a building draws its floors: each level rests on the one below and answers to the one above.
senses.whyCN: 组织安排权力就像建筑安排楼层：每一层压在下一层之上，又向上一层负责。

senses.title: The informal web behind the chart
senses.titleCN: 组织图背后的非正式网络
senses.definition: the real pattern of influence created by relationships, access and reputation rather than by titles
senses.definitionCN: 由关系、接近机会与声誉而非头衔形成的真实影响力格局
senses.example: Informal power structures often matter more than the printed chart.
senses.exampleCN: 非正式的权力结构常常比印出来的组织图更重要。
senses.why: A building has hidden corridors as well as official stairs; influence travels through both.
senses.whyCN: 建筑除了正式楼梯还有隐蔽通道；影响力也沿两条路流动。

senses.title: The division of constitutional powers
senses.definition: the arrangement that assigns authority to separate branches or levels of government
senses.definitionCN: 把权限分配给不同政府分支或层级的安排
senses.example: The constitutional power structure divides authority among three branches.
senses.exampleCN: 宪制权力结构把权限分给三个分支。
senses.why: Political theory uses the word for the architecture of a state, where each branch is a load-bearing wall.
senses.whyCN: 政治理论用这个词指国家的建筑结构，每个分支都是一面承重墙。

senses.title: Who decides inside a household
senses.definition: the pattern of decision-making and influence among members of a family or household
senses.definitionCN: 家庭成员之间作决定与施加影响的格局
senses.example: In many households the power structure shifts when an elder moves in.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多家庭里，长辈搬进来之后，权力结构就会改变。
senses.why: The same architecture appears at a smaller scale: every group that shares a roof also shares a way of deciding.
senses.whyCN: 同样的建筑结构以更小的尺度出现：每个共住一个屋檐下的群体，也共享一套作决定的方式。

senses.title: Control written into ownership
senses.titleCN: 写进股权安排的控股权
senses.definition: the way share classes, voting rules and board seats fix who controls a company
senses.definitionCN: 通过股份类别、投票规则与董事席位固定谁控制公司的方式
senses.example: A dual-class share system entrenches the power structure of the founding family.
senses.exampleCN: 双重股权制度巩固了创始家族的权力结构。
senses.why: Corporate law turns influence into a floor plan: certain shares carry keys to certain rooms.
senses.whyCN: 公司法把影响力变成一张楼层图：某些股份带着某些房间的钥匙。

senses.title: The order between states
senses.definition: the distribution of military, economic and diplomatic power among states in a region or the world
senses.definitionCN: 军事、经济与外交力量在一个地区或全世界各国之间的分布
senses.example: The postwar power structure rested on two blocs and a set of alliances.
senses.exampleCN: 战后的权力结构建立在两个阵营与一系列联盟之上。
senses.why: International relations borrows the architectural word for a balance that is built, maintained and sometimes demolished.
senses.whyCN: 国际关系借用这个建筑词汇，指一种被建造、维护、有时又被拆除的均势。

senses.title: The structure that decides whose knowledge counts
senses.titleCN: 决定谁的知识算数的结构
senses.definition: the unspoken arrangement that gives some voices the right to define problems and others no hearing
senses.definitionCN: 让某些声音有权界定问题、另一些声音却无人倾听的隐性安排
senses.example: The report questioned the power structure that decides whose expertise counts.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告质疑了决定谁的专业意见算数的权力结构。
senses.why: Even a discussion has a floor plan: some seats face the table, others face the wall.
senses.whyCN: 连一场讨论也有自己的平面图：有些座位朝向长桌，另一些只能朝向墙壁。

intro.en: Power structure joins power, from Latin posse 'to be able', with structure, from Latin structura 'a building, an arrangement', from struere 'to pile up, build'. The compound is a modern social-science term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: power structure 由 power 与 structure 组合而成。power 源自拉丁 posse「能够」；structure 源自拉丁 structura「建筑物、安排」，再往上出自 struere「堆起、建造」。这个复合词是现代社会科学术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Posse meant 'to be able', built on potis 'able' and esse 'to be'. Its pre-Latin elements are reconstructed.
items.cn: posse 意为「能够」，由 potis「有能力的」与 esse「是」构成。它在拉丁语之前的成分属于重构。

items.en: Struere meant 'to pile up, build, arrange'. Its deeper origin is not established; the building root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: struere 意为「堆起、建造、安排」。其更深来源未得到证明；为它提出的「建造」词根属于重构形式。

items.en: Structura named the act of building and the resulting arrangement, from which English took the idea of a built framework.
items.cn: structura 指建造的动作以及由此形成的安排，英语从它取得「构建起来的框架」这一观念。

items.en: Power entered English through Old French in the thirteenth century; structure came from Latin in the fifteenth and named both buildings and organized wholes.
items.cn: power 在十三世纪经古法语进入英语；structure 在十五世纪来自拉丁语，既指建筑，也指有组织的整体。

items.en: In the twentieth century the two words were joined to name the durable pattern of influence in a society or institution.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这两个词被组合起来，指一个社会或机构中持久的影响力格局。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin sources of potis and struere are reconstructions, and no exact first citation is fixed for the compound, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：potis 与 struere 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式；这个复合词也没有确切的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the two building blocks and their relatives; group two holds terms for an order of influence or command.
note.cn: 第一组是两个构词成分及其亲属词；第二组是表示影响力或命令秩序的术语。

entries.definition: The ability to act or compel; the compound names how that ability is arranged.
entries.definitionCN: 行动或强迫的能力；这个复合词指这种能力如何被安排。

entries.definition: A built arrangement of parts; alone it can describe a bridge as easily as an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分构建起来的安排；单独使用时既可描述桥梁，也可描述机构。

entries.definition: Relating to the arrangement of parts; structural power is power built into a system rather than held by a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与部分之间的安排有关；结构性权力是嵌入制度的权力，而非个人持有的权力。

entries.definition: To rebuild the arrangement of an organization, often changing who reports to whom.
entries.definitionCN: 重建一个组织的安排，常改变谁向谁汇报。

entries.definition: A system of levels in which each rank answers to the one above; it is one common form of power structure.
entries.definitionCN: 每一等级向上一级负责的层级体系；它是权力结构的一种常见形态。

entries.definition: The unofficial order of status and precedence in a group, often visible in small behaviours.
entries.definitionCN: 群体中非正式的地位与优先次序，常从小举动中看出来。

entries.definition: The rules and practices by which an organization or state is directed; it names the process, not the distribution.
entries.definitionCN: 指导一个组织或国家的规则与实践；指过程，而非分布。

entries.definition: A particular government or set of ruling arrangements; it is more political and less analytical than power structure.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的政府或一套统治安排；比 power structure 更政治化，分析性较弱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real roots, the real derivatives and the real institutional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实词根、真实的派生词与真实的机构搭配。

normal.en: The first word means 'to be able' and the second means 'built arrangement', so the compound is ability arranged into a lasting shape.
normal.cn: 第一个词意为「能够」，第二个词意为「建造起来的安排」，因此整个复合词就是被安排成持久形状的能力。

normal.en: The family runs power, structure, structural, structurally, restructure and infrastructure.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 power、structure、structural、structurally、restructure 与 infrastructure。

normal.en: The critical phrases are challenge the power structure, shift the power structure and reform the power structure.
normal.cn: 批判性搭配有挑战权力结构、改变权力结构与改革权力结构。

normal.en: The descriptive phrases are formal power structure and the power structure of a society.
normal.cn: 描述性搭配有正式权力结构与一个社会的权力结构。

normal.en: The same building root appears in infrastructure, which names the built supports beneath a system.
normal.cn: 同一「建造」词根出现在 infrastructure 中，那个词指体系下方建造起来的支撑设施。

abstract.en: Picture a cutaway building where the top floor has three rooms and the ground floor has a hundred.
abstract.cn: 想象一座剖面楼，顶层只有三个房间，底层却有一百个。

abstract.en: Picture arrows on a chart all pointing upward to the same small office.
abstract.cn: 想象组织图上的箭头全都指向上方的同一间小办公室。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where the seats facing the table decide what the others are allowed to say.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会议，朝向长桌的座位决定其余人能说什么。

examples.en: Reformers argued that the old power structure blocked every proposal for change.
examples.cn: 改革者认为旧的权力结构阻挠了每一项变革提案。

examples.en: The family's power structure changed after the youngest daughter took over the accounts.
examples.cn: 最小的女儿接管账目之后，这个家庭的权力结构改变了。

examples.en: Any study of a bureaucracy must map its formal and informal power structures.
examples.cn: 任何对官僚机构的研究都必须描绘其正式与非正式的权力结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「权力」加「结构」——谁在上面、谁在下面、箭头指向谁 → 权力结构、权力格局

root: power structure 由 power 与 structure 组合而成。power 源自拉丁 posse「能够」；structure 源自拉丁 structura「建筑物、安排」，再往上出自 struere「建造」。potis 与 struere 的更深来源均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one architectural image: an arrangement of levels tells who stands above whom. The arrangement is applied to a society, a company, an informal network, a constitution, a household, a shareholding scheme, the world of states and finally to the seating of a discussion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个建筑意象展开：一层层的安排说明谁站在谁之上。这个安排依次用于社会、公司、非正式网络、宪制、家庭、股权方案、国家格局，最后用于一场讨论的座次。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cutaway building with arrows running upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座剖面楼，箭头一路向上。

branches.en: THE WHOLE SHAPE: the first sense asks who holds power across a society, not in one office.
branches.cn: 整体形状：第一个义项追问整个社会中谁掌握权力，而非某一间办公室。

branches.en: THE DRAWN FLOOR PLAN: official reporting lines and share classes fix the same structure on paper.
branches.cn: 画出的楼层图：正式汇报线与股份类别在纸面上固定了同一种结构。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN PASSAGE: relationships and the right to define a problem move influence off the printed chart.
branches.cn: 隐蔽通道：关系与界定问题的权利，把影响力带离印好的组织图。

branches.en: THE LOAD-BEARING WALLS: a constitution assigns authority to separate branches so that none carries the whole roof.
branches.cn: 承重墙：宪法把权限分给不同分支，使没有任何一方独自撑起整个屋顶。

branches.en: THE SMALL AND LARGE ROOF: a household and a world of states both settle who decides under one shared frame.
branches.cn: 大小屋檐：家庭与国家格局都在同一个共享框架下确定谁作决定。

intro.en: The compound can be read from two Latin sources: a verb of ability and a verb of building, each with its own derived family.
intro.cn: 这个复合词可以按两个拉丁来源读出：一个表示能力的动词，一个表示建造的动词，各自带有派生词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse supplies power and potent; Latin struere supplies structure, structural and restructure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 posse 衍生 power 与 potent；拉丁 struere 衍生 structure、structural 与 restructure。

items.example: The verb is the source of the first element.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是第一个构词成分的来源。

items.example: Power is the first element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: power 是这个复合词的第一个成分。

items.structure: struere, struxi, structum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the image of building.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供建造的意象。

items.example: The noun named both a building and its plan.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指建筑，也指它的布局。

items.example: The second element names the arrangement.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分指这种安排。

items.example: Structural change altered the reporting lines.
items.exampleCN: 结构性变化改变了汇报线。

items.example: The agency is structurally dependent on the ministry.
items.exampleCN: 该机构在结构上依赖部里。

items.example: The firm restructured its regional offices.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司重组了地区办事处。

items.meaning: the built supports beneath a system
items.example: Roads and pipes form the infrastructure of the town.
items.exampleCN: 道路与管道构成这座镇的基础设施。

senses.example: Children need calcium for growing bones.

senses.why: Chemistry named the element, and everyday use focuses on the mineral in living things.
senses.whyCN: 化学命名了元素，而日常用法多指生物体内的矿物质。

intro.en: Calcium was named in 1808 from Latin calx, the word for lime.
intro.cn: calcium 于一八零八年依拉丁语 calx（石灰）命名。

items.cn: calx 意为石灰或白垩。

items.cn: 一八零八年戴维分离出这种金属。

definition_zh: 到来；出现；（首字母大写）基督降临节
definition_en: the arrival or first appearance of something important, especially after a long wait
core_image: 远处的地平线上终于出现一个正在靠近的黑点
scene: 天文台的观测窗前，一群人守到后半夜，屏幕上的光点终于开始变大。 The advent of cheap sensors changed amateur astronomy completely.
sceneCN: 这里 advent 是「到来」（第 1 个义项：重要事物经过漫长等待后出现）；句意为廉价传感器的到来彻底改变了业余天文。图中可辨识的物件：望远镜、屏幕、保温杯。

pos.zh: 到来；出现；（大写）基督降临节

forms.label: 不可数（固定于 the advent of）

derivatives.zh: 由 Advent 加 -ist 构成，指「相信基督再临的教派成员」
由同一拉丁词根加 -itious 构成，义为「偶然外来的；非本位的」
由 Advent 加 -al 构成，义为「降临节的」

senses.title: The arrival of something long awaited
senses.definition: the arrival of an important event, thing or period after a period of waiting
senses.definitionCN: 重要的事件、事物或时期经过一段等待之后的到来
senses.example: The advent of the printing press reshaped reading in Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷机的到来重塑了欧洲的阅读方式。
senses.why: The Latin noun means an arrival, so the plainest sense is simply that something has come.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本义就是「到达」，所以最朴素的义项就是某物已经来了。

senses.title: The first appearance of a technology
senses.definition: the point at which a new tool, product or system first becomes available
senses.definitionCN: 新的工具、产品或系统首次可供使用的时点
senses.example: The advent of streaming ended the video shop on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 流媒体的出现终结了街角的录像店。
senses.why: When an invention arrives it divides time into before and after, so the word marks a boundary in history.
senses.whyCN: 一项发明到来时把时间分成前后两段，所以这个词标记的是历史上的一道分界。

senses.title: The Christian season before Christmas
senses.definition: the four weeks of preparation before Christmas in the Christian calendar
senses.definitionCN: 基督教历法中圣诞节前为期四周的准备期
senses.example: The church stays unlit during Advent until the fourth Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 降临节期间，教堂直到第四个主日才点灯。
senses.why: The season is named for a coming, because it is spent waiting for a birth that has not yet happened.
senses.whyCN: 这个节期以「到来」命名，因为它整个是在等待一件尚未发生的诞生。

senses.title: The expected return of Christ
senses.definition: in theology, the promised second coming of Christ at the end of history
senses.definitionCN: 神学中，历史终结时基督应许的第二次来临
senses.example: The sermon dwelt on the advent of the Lord in judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲道详述了主在审判中的再临。
senses.why: The same noun serves the liturgical calendar and the end of time, both being arrivals that the faithful wait for.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既服务礼仪年历，也服务时间的终点，两者都是信徒等待的来临。

senses.title: The start of a new era
senses.definition: the beginning of a new period in a field or in society
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或社会中一个新时期的开始
senses.example: Historians speak of the advent of the industrial age.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家谈到工业时代的到来。
senses.why: An arrival can be large enough to name an age, and the word then stands for the opening of a period.
senses.whyCN: 一次到来可以大到足以命名一个时代，此时这个词就代指一个时期的开端。

senses.title: A person's arrival in a role
senses.definition: in formal or literary use, the arrival of a notable person into a place or post
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学用法中，某位重要人物进入某地或某职
senses.example: The advent of a new coach lifted the whole squad.
senses.exampleCN: 新教练的到任提振了整支队伍。
senses.why: People also arrive, and formal prose borrows the grand noun to give an entrance some weight.
senses.whyCN: 人也会到达，正式文字借用这个庄重的名词，给一次登场添上分量。

senses.title: The onset of a condition
senses.definition: in medical writing, the point at which a disease or symptom begins
senses.definitionCN: 医学写作中，疾病或症状开始出现的时点
senses.example: Treatment works best before the advent of severe symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 在严重症状出现之前治疗效果最好。
senses.why: A disease arrives on its own schedule, so medicine uses the same noun for the hour it first shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 疾病按自己的时间表到来，于是医学用同一个名词指它初次露面的时刻。

senses.title: The coming of a season
senses.definition: in literary description, the arrival of a season or a natural change
senses.definitionCN: 在文学描写中，季节或自然变化的来临
senses.example: The advent of spring brought colour back to the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 春天的来临让山谷重新有了颜色。
senses.why: Seasons come whether or not anyone waits, and poetry keeps the old noun for that quiet arrival.
senses.whyCN: 季节无论有没有人等待都会来，诗歌便用这个古老的名词指那种安静的来临。

intro.en: Advent is the Latin noun adventus, an arrival, from advenire, to come to, built on venire, to come.
intro.cn: advent 是拉丁名词 adventus「到达」，来自 advenire「来到」，其基础是 venire「来」。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it also feeds English venue, avenue and prevent.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，英语的 venue、avenue 与 prevent 也由它而来。

items.en: Ad plus venire gave advenire, to come to or arrive at a place.
items.cn: ad 加 venire 构成 advenire，意为「来到」或「抵达某地」。

items.en: The fourth-declension noun adventus named the arrival itself, whether of a person, a season or a god.
items.cn: 第四变格名词 adventus 命名到达本身，无论到的是人、季节还是神。

items.en: Old French took the word as avent, and English borrowed it first in ecclesiastical texts.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带作 avent，英语最先在教会文本中借入。

items.en: The liturgical sense is the earliest in English; the general sense of any arrival develops later.
items.cn: 英语中最早的义项是礼仪上的节期，泛指的「任何到来」则发展得较晚。

items.en: Modern usage splits the lowercase general noun from the capitalised season, a distinction kept in print.
items.cn: 现代用法把小写的泛指名词与大写的节期分开，印刷中一直保留这一区别。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same venire family, two of which have drifted far from plain arrival; the near-meaning group gathers plainer words for coming, which differ in register and in what they name.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 venire 词族的词，其中两个已远离「到达」的本义；近义组收表示「来临」的更朴素说法，差别在于语体与所指。

entries.definition: From Latin adventura, things about to happen, but now meaning a risky journey rather than a coming.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语 adventura「即将发生之事」，但今义是冒险旅程，而非到来。

entries.definition: A botanical and medical adjective meaning arriving from outside rather than by nature.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学与医学形容词，指从外部而非本性带来的。

entries.definition: A member of a church that centres on the expected second coming.
entries.definitionCN: 以期待基督再临为核心的教会成员。

entries.definition: The plain word for reaching a place, used of people and trains more often than of eras.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某地的朴素说法，多用于人与列车，而非时代。

entries.definition: A general noun for something approaching, without the formality or grandeur of advent.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某物临近的名词，没有 advent 的正式或庄重感。

entries.definition: The beginning of something unpleasant, especially a disease or winter.
entries.definitionCN: 不愉快之事的开始，尤指疾病或冬季。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb venire, the word family and the fixed phrases the noun forms in English.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁动词 venire、这个词族，以及这个名词在英语中构成的固定短语。

normal.en: Venire means to come, and ad adds direction: advenire is to come toward, so advent is the coming.
normal.cn: venire 意为「来」，ad 加上方向：advenire 就是「朝这边来」，所以 advent 就是「到来」。

normal.en: Venire is also hiding in venue, avenue and prevent, all about coming or blocking a coming.
normal.cn: venire 还藏在 venue、avenue 与 prevent 里，都与「来」或「挡住来」有关。

normal.en: The standard frame is the advent of something: the advent of the internet, the advent of cheap sensors.
normal.cn: 标准框架是 the advent of 某物：the advent of the internet、the advent of cheap sensors。

normal.en: Capitalised, Advent is the four weeks before Christmas, counted with an Advent calendar.
normal.cn: 首字母大写时，Advent 是圣诞节前的四周，用降临节日历一天天倒数。

normal.en: Before the advent of is the phrase for the world that existed earlier.
normal.cn: before the advent of 是描述「更早那个世界」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a ship sighted from a cliff: first a dot, then a mast, then a whole hull.
abstract.cn: 想象从悬崖上望见一艘船：先是黑点，然后是桅杆，最后是整个船身。

abstract.en: An advent cuts history in two, which is why the word can name an age as easily as a gadget.
abstract.cn: 一次到来把历史切成两段，所以这个词既能命名一个时代，也能命名一件小器具。

abstract.en: The liturgical sense survives because waiting is still the shape of the season.
abstract.cn: 礼仪上的义项之所以留存，是因为等待仍然是这个节期的形状。

examples.en: The advent of online banking closed hundreds of small branches.
examples.cn: 网上银行的到来让数百家小分行关门。

examples.en: Before the advent of the railway, the journey took three days.
examples.cn: 在铁路出现之前，这段路程要走三天。

examples.en: The choir rehearses throughout Advent for the midnight service.
examples.cn: 唱诗班在整个降临节期间为午夜礼拜排练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德文特」——阿德闻声而至：到来

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ venire（来）→ advenire「来到」→ 名词 adventus「到达」，英语作 advent，指重要事物的到来，也指圣诞节前的降临节。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advent all describe something crossing the horizon: an awaited thing, a new technology, the church season, the final return, a new era, a person's arrival, the onset of illness and the coming of spring.
sensesIntro.cn: advent 的八个义项都描述某物越过地平线：被等待的事物、新技术、教会的节期、最终的再临、新时代、某人的到任、病症的发作，以及春天的来临。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dot on the horizon growing until it is unmistakably here.
core.cn: 核心意象：地平线上的黑点不断变大，直到它确凿无疑地到了。

branches.en: THE ARRIVAL LINE: the plain coming and the first appearance of a tool are the same event seen close up.
branches.cn: 到来线：朴素的来临与一件工具的首次出现，是同一事件被拉近观看。

branches.en: THE SACRED LINE: the season and the second coming both turn waiting into a calendar.
branches.cn: 神圣线：节期与再临都把等待变成一份日历。

branches.en: THE EPOCH LINE: a large enough arrival becomes the name of an age.
branches.cn: 时代线：一次足够大的到来会变成时代的名字。

branches.en: THE ENTRANCE LINE: people and diseases alike make their entrance on the same noun.
branches.cn: 登场线：人与疾病都用同一个名词完成自己的登场。

branches.en: THE SEASON LINE: spring arrives without waiting, and the old noun still fits.
branches.cn: 季节线：春天并不等待谁就来了，而这个古老名词依然合用。

intro.en: Advent is a Latin fourth-declension noun from advenire; English keeps the -vent stem and builds -ist, -itious and -al on it.
intro.cn: advent 是来自 advenire 的拉丁第四变格名词；英语保留 -vent 词干，并在其上构成 -ist、-itious 与 -al。

latinIntro.en: Venire, advenire and adventus are all attested in Latin, so the chain needs no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: venire、advenire 与 adventus 在拉丁语中均有文献，这条链条无需构拟。

items.example: It turns venire into a coming toward.
items.exampleCN: 它把 venire 变成「朝这边来」。

items.example: It is the semantic core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族的意义核心。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It appears in advent, event and prevent.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 advent、event 与 prevent 中。
