由同一词根加 -itious 构成，义为「偶然外来的」

definition_zh: 碱性；碱度；（水的）总碱度（抵偿酸的能力）
definition_en: the quality or degree of being alkaline, or the measured capacity of water to neutralise acid
core_image: 一只水样瓶旁摆着滴定管与色卡，滴到颜色定住的那一刻，读数才被写下
scene: 检测员把酸液滴进水样，直到颜色停住不动，然后写下这口井的碱度。 The alkalinity of the well water was tested before the fish ponds were stocked.
sceneCN: 这里 alkalinity 指水呈碱性、能抵偿酸的程度（第 2 个义项：水的总碱度）；句意：在鱼塘放养之前，先测了这口井水的碱度。图中可辨识物件：水样瓶、滴定管、比色卡、记录表。

derivatives.zh: 由 alkali 加形容词词尾构成，义为「碱性的」
由 alkali 加使动词尾构成，义为「使碱化」
由 alkali 加医学病态词尾构成，义为「碱中毒」
由 alkali 加表示测量的成分构成，义为「碱度计」

senses.title: The quality of being alkaline
senses.definition: the character a substance has when it behaves as a base rather than an acid
senses.definitionCN: 某物质表现为碱而非酸时所具有的性质
senses.example: Farmers judge the alkalinity of the soil before choosing a crop.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在选择作物之前先判断土壤的碱性。
senses.why: The noun is the quality form of the adjective, so its first sense is simply the state of being alkaline.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是形容词的性质形式，因此第一个义项就是「呈碱性」这一状态。

senses.title: Water's capacity to absorb acid
senses.definition: the measured ability of water to neutralise added acid without a large change in pH, supplied mainly by carbonate and bicarbonate
senses.definitionCN: 水在加入酸后不使酸碱度大幅变化的能力，主要来自碳酸盐与碳酸氢盐
senses.example: The alkalinity of the well water was tested before the fish ponds were stocked.
senses.exampleCN: 在鱼塘放养之前，先测了这口井水的碱度。
senses.why: Water engineers care less about the label than about how much acid the water can swallow, so the noun became a capacity.
senses.whyCN: 水处理工程师关心的不只是标签，而是水能吞下多少酸，于是这个名词变成了一种能力。

senses.title: The basic condition of soil
senses.definition: the degree to which soil is basic, which controls nutrient availability and which crops can be grown
senses.definitionCN: 土壤偏碱的程度，决定养分有效性以及能种哪些作物
senses.example: High alkalinity locked iron out of reach of the plants.
senses.exampleCN: 高碱度使铁无法被植物吸收。
senses.why: Agriculture applies the measured sense to land, where the number predicts what will flourish.
senses.whyCN: 农业把可测量的义项用在土地上，那里的数字能预示什么会长得好。

senses.title: The sea's built-in buffer
senses.definition: the capacity of seawater to resist changes in pH, which keeps marine life stable
senses.definitionCN: 海水抵抗酸碱度变化的能力，使海洋生物得以稳定生存
senses.example: Decades of measurement show the ocean's alkalinity slowly shifting.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年测量显示海洋的碱度正在缓慢变化。
senses.why: Oceanography treats the capacity as a global property, because the buffer is what keeps a whole ecosystem from swinging.
senses.whyCN: 海洋学把这种能力当作全球尺度上的性质，因为正是这层缓冲让整个生态系统免于剧烈摆动。

senses.title: The number from a titration
senses.definition: the figure obtained by adding acid of known strength until the sample reaches a chosen end point
senses.definitionCN: 加入已知强度的酸直到样品到达选定终点所得到的数值
senses.example: The alkalinity test gave a value of two hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 碱度测定给出两百这个数值。
senses.why: Because the capacity can be spent exactly by a measured acid, it can be reported as a number in a logbook.
senses.whyCN: 既然这种能力可以被已知量的酸正好用掉，它就能作为数字记进记录本。

senses.title: A control target in pools and boilers
senses.titleCN: 水池与锅炉里的控制指标
senses.definition: the level of alkalinity kept within a set range so that equipment is protected and treatment works
senses.definitionCN: 为使设备受保护、处理生效而维持在设定范围内的碱度水平
senses.example: The operator raised the alkalinity to stop the pipes corroding.
senses.exampleCN: 操作员提高碱度以阻止管道腐蚀。
senses.why: Industry turns the measurement into a dial to be held steady, so the noun names a target rather than a natural fact.
senses.whyCN: 工业把测量变成一个要稳定握住的旋钮，于是这个名词命名一个目标，而非自然事实。

senses.title: A feature of lakes and streams
senses.definition: the basic character of a freshwater body, which shapes which species can live there
senses.definitionCN: 淡水水体的碱性格，决定哪些物种能生存
senses.example: The alkalinity of the stream fell after the mine opened.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场开工后，溪水的碱度下降了。
senses.why: Field surveys use the word as a lasting trait of a place, not a single reading.
senses.whyCN: 野外调查把这个词当作某地持久的特点，而不是一次读数。

senses.title: The opposite side of the acid measure
senses.definition: the mirror quantity to acidity, describing how far a solution leans toward base
senses.definitionCN: 与酸度相对的镜像量，描述溶液偏向碱的程度
senses.example: Chemists reported both acidity and alkalinity for the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家为样品同时报告了酸度与碱度。
senses.why: The two nouns divide the same scale between them, so each names the distance from neutral in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 这两个名词把同一条尺度分成两半，各自命名从中性朝一个方向走出的距离。

intro.en: Alkalinity is alkali plus a quality ending, formed in the eighteenth century as chemistry needed a noun for the measured property. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: alkalinity 是 alkali 加性质名词词尾构成，出现于 18 世纪，当时化学需要一个名词来指这一可测量的性质。年代为约数。

items.en: The root is Arabic al-qily, the ashes of a salt-tolerant plant burned to make a cleansing substance.
items.cn: 词根是阿拉伯语 al-qily，指一种耐盐植物烧成的灰，用于制作清洗物质。

items.en: Medieval Latin adopted the term for the soda and potash substances that early chemists handled.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语借入该词，指早期化学家处理的苏打与碳酸钾类物质。

items.en: English took alkali in the seventeenth century, and the adjective alkaline followed in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 alkali，形容词 alkaline 于 18 世纪随后出现。

items.en: The quality noun added an ending that turns an adjective into a measurable state, so the word could enter titration records.
items.cn: 性质名词加上一个把形容词变成可测状态的词尾，于是这个词得以进入滴定记录。

items.en: Water treatment, pool care and boiler operation turned the measurement into a controlled target in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 水处理、泳池维护与锅炉运行在 20 世纪把这项测量变成受控指标。

items.en: Source uncertain for details: the exact plant behind the Arabic root is not securely established, and the noun's earliest English citation is not fixed either.
items.cn: 细节来源不确定：词根所指的确切阿拉伯植物未被牢固确立，该名词最早的英语引文同样未被固定。

note.en: The first group shares the alkali stem and differs by word class; the second group is the opposite measure and the instruments around it.
note.cn: 第一组共享 alkali 词干而词类不同；第二组是相对的度量与周围的仪器。

entries.definition: Having a pH above seven; it labels a substance, while alkalinity measures how strongly it does so.
entries.definitionCN: 酸碱度高于七；它给物质贴标签，而 alkalinity 测量其程度。

entries.definition: A soluble base; it is a thing, not a measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 可溶性碱；它是物质，不是度量。

entries.definition: To make something alkaline; it names an action, while the noun names a state.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变碱；它命名动作，而名词命名状态。

entries.definition: The titration that produces the number; here the noun is a modifier inside the name of a method.
entries.definitionCN: 产生该数值的滴定；这里该名词是方法名称里的修饰成分。

entries.definition: The measured degree of being acid; it points the other way along the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 所测的呈酸程度；它在同一条尺度上指向另一端。

entries.definition: The number of protons a base can accept, or the number of replaceable hydrogens in an acid; it counts capacity per molecule, not water's buffering.
entries.definitionCN: 一个碱能接受的质子数，或一种酸中可被置换的氢原子数；它按分子计数，而不是水的缓冲能力。

entries.definition: The resistance of a solution to pH change; alkalinity is one source of it, but the word names the behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 溶液抵抗酸碱度变化的能力；碱度是其来源之一，但这个词命名的是行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: alkaline plus the quality ending: the measured state of being basic.
normal.cn: alkaline 加性质词尾：呈碱这一可测状态。

normal.en: The family runs alkali, alkaline, alkalinity, alkalize, alkalosis.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 alkali、alkaline、alkalinity、alkalize、alkalosis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the water side: total alkalinity, water alkalinity, alkalinity test.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出与水有关的一面：总碱度、水的碱度、碱度测定。

normal.en: Water engineers treat it as how much acid the water can swallow.
normal.cn: 水处理工程师把它看作「水能吞下多少酸」。

normal.en: Acidity and alkalinity divide the same scale at the neutral point.
normal.cn: 酸度与碱度在中性点把同一条尺度分成两半。

abstract.en: Picture a sponge that soaks up spilled vinegar without letting the puddle spread.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵吸掉泼出的醋，不让水洼扩大。

abstract.en: Picture a lake that keeps its mood steady while rain of different kinds falls on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片湖，各种雨水落进去，它的脾气却保持稳定。

abstract.en: Picture a gauge the operator watches and turns until the needle sits in the safe band.
abstract.cn: 想象操作员盯着一个表盘，把指针调进安全的那一段。

examples.en: The lab reports total alkalinity alongside pH for every sample.
examples.cn: 实验室为每个样品同时报告总碱度与酸碱度。

examples.en: Low alkalinity made the stream vulnerable to acid rain.
examples.cn: 低碱度使这条溪流容易受酸雨影响。

examples.en: Operators check alkalinity twice a day in the cooling tower.
examples.cn: 操作员每天在冷却塔检查碱度两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「alkaline（碱性）+ ity（程度）」——碱的程度，就是碱度

root: 阿拉伯 al-qily「盐生植物的灰」→ 中世纪拉丁 alkali → 英语 alkali、alkaline + 表示性质的名词词尾；指碱性或可测的总碱度。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one basic capacity: the quality itself, water's ability to absorb acid, the soil verdict, the sea's buffer, the titration number, an industrial target, a whole stream, and the mirror half of the acid scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种碱的能力：性质本身、水抵偿酸的能力、土壤判断、海洋缓冲、滴定数值、工业指标、整条溪流，以及酸度尺度上的镜像那一半。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: acid dripped into a sample until the colour holds, and only then is the figure written.
core.cn: 核心意象：酸滴进样品，直到颜色定住，这时才写下数字。

branches.en: THE QUALITY AND ITS MIRROR: the state of being basic, and the half of the scale that faces acidity.
branches.cn: 性质及其镜像：呈碱的状态，以及尺度上与酸度相对的那一半。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND NUMBER: how much acid the water can take, and the figure a titration writes down.
branches.cn: 能力与数字：水能承受多少酸，以及滴定写下的数值。

branches.en: THE LAND: the same capacity decides which nutrients stay reachable in a field.
branches.cn: 土地：同一种能力决定田里哪些养分仍可被够到。

branches.en: THE WIDE WATER: a sea and a stream both hold a basic character that keeps life steady.
branches.cn: 广阔的水：海与溪都保有碱的性格，使生命保持稳定。

branches.en: THE DIAL: in a plant the capacity becomes a range that must be held, not merely observed.
branches.cn: 表盘：在工厂里，这种能力变成一个必须维持的范围，而不只是被观察。

intro.en: Alkalinity is an Arabic-derived noun plus a quality ending, and the family covers chemistry, water treatment and medicine.
intro.cn: alkalinity 是一个阿拉伯语来源的名词加性质词尾，词族覆盖化学、水处理与医学。

latinIntro.en: The root is Arabic and reached Europe through medieval Latin; Latin supplies only the endings, so no Latin root relative is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自阿拉伯语，经中世纪拉丁语传入欧洲；拉丁语只提供词尾，因此不列词根的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The root names the ashes used for cleansing.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名用于清洗的灰。

items.meaning: having the character of an alkali

items.structure: noun ending for state or quality
items.example: The ending makes the property measurable.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使该性质可被测量。

items.meaning: the measured state of being basic

items.structure: alkali plus a medical state ending
items.exampleCN: 长时间呕吐后可能出现碱中毒。

items.example: The alkalimeter replaced the older titration.
items.exampleCN: 碱度计取代了较早的滴定法。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「碱性的」
由基础名词加使动词尾构成，义为「使碱化」

definition_zh: 温盐环流；由温度与盐度差异驱动的全球深层海洋环流
definition_en: the large-scale overturning circulation of the ocean, driven by differences in seawater temperature and salinity and moving deep water between basins over centuries
core_image: 极地海面结冰析出盐分，剩水更冷更咸而下沉，沿深海铺展到远处，再从另一侧缓缓升回海面，绕成一圈
scene: 气候课上，老师沿着全球海图画出从北大西洋下沉、绕过南极再回到北太平洋的长箭头说， Thermohaline circulation returns deep water to the surface centuries later.
sceneCN: 这里 thermohaline circulation 指「由温度与盐度差异驱动的全球深层海洋环流」（第 1 个义项：总称）；句意为：温盐环流在数百年之后才把深层水送回海面。

derivatives.zh: 大西洋经向翻转环流（该环流在大西洋的系统）
翻转环流；深层水上翻、表层水下沉的环流
经向翻转；沿南北方向的垂直翻转
传送带（对这一全球环流系统的比喻称呼）
深层水形成；表层水下沉成为深层水的环节

senses.title: The overturning loop as a whole
senses.definition: the global-scale circulation in which dense water sinks in a few cold regions and returns to the surface elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 高密度水在少数寒冷海域下沉、又在别处回到表层的全球尺度环流
senses.example: Thermohaline circulation links all the major ocean basins.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐环流把所有主要海盆连在一起。
senses.why: the compound names its own cause: heat and salt make the density differences, and circulation names the loop those differences produce.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词点明了自己的成因：热与盐造成密度差，circulation 则指这些差异所生成的环路。

senses.title: The sinking limb
senses.definition: the part of the loop where surface water cools, becomes dense and descends
senses.definitionCN: 环路中表层水冷却、变重并下潜的那一段
senses.example: The sinking limb of thermohaline circulation begins in the northern Atlantic.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐环流的下沉支始于北大西洋北部。
senses.why: a loop has to start somewhere, and it starts where water can lose heat fast enough to become heavier than what lies beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 环路总得从某处开始，而它开始于水能迅速失热、重到超过下方水体的地方。

senses.title: The returning limb
senses.definition: the part of the loop in which deep water travels through the basins and slowly rises
senses.definitionCN: 环路中深层水穿行各海盆并缓慢上升的那一段
senses.example: The returning limb of thermohaline circulation is spread over the whole Indian and Pacific oceans.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐环流的回流支分布在整个印度洋与太平洋。
senses.why: water that went down must come up before it can go down again, and this long return takes most of the loop's travel time.
senses.whyCN: 下去的水必须先上来才能再下去，而这段漫长的回程占去了环路的大部分行程时间。

senses.title: The conveyor belt image
senses.definition: the popular image of the loop as a single belt carrying water, heat and carbon around the globe
senses.definitionCN: 把环路想象成绕地球输送水、热量与碳的一条传送带的流行说法
senses.example: The conveyor belt image made thermohaline circulation familiar outside oceanography.
senses.exampleCN: 传送带这一意象使温盐环流在海洋学之外也为人熟知。
senses.why: no observer can watch a loop that takes centuries, so it is drawn as a belt with stations, and that is how it entered textbooks.
senses.whyCN: 没人能观看一个耗时数百年的环路，于是它被画成带站点的传送带，也就这样进入了教科书。

senses.title: A heat transport system
senses.definition: the loop considered as the mechanism that redistributes heat between the tropics and the poles
senses.definitionCN: 被视作在热带与极地之间重新分配热量的机制
senses.example: Thermohaline circulation keeps the northern Atlantic warmer than its latitude alone would allow.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐环流使北大西洋比单凭纬度所能允许的更暖。
senses.why: the same water that carries salt carries heat, so the loop works as a heating system with an ocean for pipes.
senses.whyCN: 载盐的水同时载热，因此这个环路像一套以海洋为管道的供暖系统。

senses.title: A carrier of carbon and nutrients
senses.definition: the loop considered as a conveyor of dissolved carbon, oxygen and nutrients into the deep sea
senses.definitionCN: 被视作把溶解碳、氧与营养盐送入深海的输送系统
senses.example: Thermohaline circulation buries carbon in the deep ocean for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐环流把碳封存在深海中数百年。
senses.why: deep water is out of contact with the air, so whatever it carries down stays down until the loop brings it back.
senses.whyCN: 深层水与大气隔绝，因此它带下去的东西一直留在下面，直到环路把它带回来。

senses.title: A cell in a climate model
senses.titleCN: 气候模式中的环流单元
senses.definition: the overturning cell represented in a numerical model of the ocean and climate
senses.definitionCN: 在海洋与气候数值模式中被表示出来的翻转单元
senses.example: The model's thermohaline circulation weakens when fresh water is added at high latitudes.
senses.exampleCN: 当高纬地区淡水增加时，模式中的温盐环流会减弱。
senses.why: a model cannot hold a whole ocean, so the loop is reduced to a cell with a strength number attached.
senses.whyCN: 模式装不下整个海洋，于是环路被简化为一个带强度数值的单元。

senses.title: A past state of the loop
senses.definition: a particular mode of the loop reconstructed for a past climate, such as a weaker glacial mode
senses.definitionCN: 为过去气候重建出的环路特定状态，如较弱的冰期状态
senses.example: Proxy records suggest that thermohaline circulation slowed during the cold period.
senses.exampleCN: 代用指标记录显示温盐环流在寒冷期减慢。
senses.why: the loop leaves traces in sediment and ice, so it can be reconstructed as a state and not only observed as a present process.
senses.whyCN: 环流在沉积物与冰中留下痕迹，因此它能被重建为一种状态，而不只是被观测为当下的过程。

senses.title: A very slow clock
senses.definition: the centennial to millennial timescale on which the loop responds to change
senses.definitionCN: 环路对变化作出响应的百年至千年尺度
senses.example: On the thermohaline circulation's own clock, the recent warming is almost instantaneous.
senses.exampleCN: 按温盐环流自身的时间尺度看，近期的变暖几乎是瞬间发生的。
senses.why: water in the loop takes centuries to complete a circuit, so any change in it is read in centuries rather than in seasons.
senses.whyCN: 环路中的水要数百年才走完一圈，因此它的任何变化都以百年而非季节来度量。

intro.en: Thermohaline circulation joins a Greek-based adjective to a Latin-based noun: thermohaline from thermē 'heat' and halinos 'of salt', circulation from Latin circulatio, a going round. The phrase is a twentieth-century oceanographic compound. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: thermohaline circulation 把一个希腊系形容词与一个拉丁系名词组合起来：thermohaline 出自 thermē「热」与 halinos「盐的」，circulation 出自拉丁 circulatio「绕行」。这一短语是 20 世纪海洋学的复合术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Thermohaline, built in the nineteenth century from thermē 'heat' and halinos 'of salt', supplied the adjective that names the cause of the density differences.
items.cn: thermohaline 于 19 世纪由 thermē「热」与 halinos「盐的」构成，提供了命名密度差异成因的形容词。

items.en: Circulatio comes from circulus 'small ring' and the verb circulare 'to move in a circle'; Latin used it for anything that returns to its starting point.
items.cn: circulatio 来自 circulus「小圆圈」与动词 circulare「绕圈运动」；拉丁语用它指任何回到起点的运动。

items.en: English circulation is recorded from the sixteenth century for movement in a circle, and was extended to the blood and later to the air and the sea.
items.cn: 英语 circulation 的书证见于 16 世纪，指绕圈运动，后来扩展到血液，再扩展到空气与海洋。

items.en: Physical oceanographers of the mid-twentieth century needed a name for the density-driven overturning that wind-driven theory could not explain, and the two existing words were joined.
items.cn: 20 世纪中期的物理海洋学家需要一个名称，指风驱动理论无法解释的密度驱动翻转，于是把两个已有的词拼在一起。

items.en: The phrase spread beyond specialist literature when the loop was popularised as a great conveyor belt in the late twentieth century; that image, not a new coinage, made the term public.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，这个环路被通俗化为一条巨大的传送带，该短语因而走出专业文献；使这一术语走向公众的是那个意象，而不是新造的词语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first use of the full phrase, not the roots): the exact first appearance and author are not established, and the attribution of the conveyor image to any single paper is generally accepted but not documented step by step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指完整短语的首见，不涉及词根）：最早出现的时间与作者没有定论；传送带意象归于某篇论文的说法属于「一般认为是」，但缺少逐步文献。

note.en: Group one holds the adjective alone and the broader or mechanism-neutral names built from the same words; group two holds specific branches and parts of the same system.
note.cn: 第一组是单独使用的形容词，以及由同样词汇构成、范围更宽或机制中性的名称；第二组是同一系统中的具体分支与部件。

entries.definition: the adjective describes the heat-and-salt cause; it does not by itself name the loop, which needs circulation.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词描述热与盐的成因；它本身并不命名环路，环路还要靠 circulation。

entries.definition: the whole system of ocean flow, wind-driven and density-driven alike; thermohaline circulation is only its density-driven part.
entries.definitionCN: 指海洋流动的整个系统，风驱动与密度驱动都算；温盐环流只是其中密度驱动的部分。

entries.definition: a circulation described by its up-and-down motion rather than its cause; it can be driven by heat, salt, wind or tides.
entries.definitionCN: 按上下运动而非按成因描述的环流；它可由热、盐、风或潮汐驱动。

entries.definition: the usual abbreviation of thermohaline circulation in tables and figures; it saves space, not meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 温盐环流在图表中的常用缩写；它省的是篇幅，不是含义。

entries.definition: the Atlantic meridional overturning circulation; it is the Atlantic part of the global loop, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 大西洋经向翻转环流；它是全球环路中的大西洋部分，而不是全部。

entries.definition: the teaching image of the loop, not a formal term; it stresses transport and underplays the return path.
entries.definitionCN: 环路的教学意象，不是正式术语；它强调输送，而对回程有所淡化。

entries.definition: the horizontal wind-driven loops within a basin; they lie above the overturning and are driven differently.
entries.definitionCN: 海盆内由风驱动的水平环路；它们位于翻转之上，成因也不同。

entries.definition: the process by which surface water becomes dense enough to sink; it is the start of the loop rather than the loop.
entries.definitionCN: 表层水变得足够重而下沉的过程；它是环路的起点，而不是环路本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Break it in two: thermohaline names the cause (heat and salt), circulation names the loop.
normal.cn: 拆成两半看：thermohaline 命名成因（热与盐），circulation 命名环路。

normal.en: circulation is from Latin circulus 'small ring': the water ends where it started, centuries later.
normal.cn: circulation 来自拉丁 circulus「小圆圈」：水在数百年后回到它出发的地方。

normal.en: Its parts are fixed: sinking limb, returning limb, deep water formation.
normal.cn: 它的部件是固定的：下沉支、回流支、深层水形成。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: weakening of thermohaline circulation, thermohaline circulation shutdown, thermohaline circulation model.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：温盐环流减弱、温盐环流停止、温盐环流模式。

normal.en: The abbreviation THC is the same thing in less space; AMOC is only its Atlantic branch.
normal.cn: 缩写 THC 是同一事物的简短写法；AMOC 只是它的大西洋分支。

abstract.en: Picture a loop drawn on a map that no ship could finish in a human lifetime.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画着一个环路，没有船能在人的一生中走完。

abstract.en: Picture a belt with stations, turning so slowly that the movement is invisible.
abstract.cn: 想象一条带站点的传送带，慢到看不出它在动。

abstract.en: Picture cold salty water at the rim of the world, deciding to go down.
abstract.cn: 想象世界边缘又冷又咸的水，决定下沉。

examples.en: Thermohaline circulation is driven by density, not by wind.
examples.cn: 温盐环流由密度驱动，而不是由风驱动。

examples.en: A shutdown of thermohaline circulation would change climates far from the Atlantic.
examples.cn: 温盐环流一旦停止，远离大西洋的气候也会改变。

examples.en: Scientists compare model thermohaline circulation with traces left in sediments.
examples.cn: 科学家把模式中的温盐环流与沉积物里留下的痕迹作比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「热·盐·转圈」——热与盐让水变重下沉，绕地球转一大圈 → 温盐环流

root: thermohaline（希腊 thermē「热」+ halinos「盐的」+ 后缀 -ine）+ circulation（拉丁 circulus「小圆圈」→ circulatio「绕圈运转」，经古法语进入英语）；20 世纪海洋学复合术语，指密度驱动的全球翻转环流；拉丁 circulus 的印欧来源为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one loop: the whole circuit, the cold place where it sinks, the long way back, the belt drawn in textbooks, the heat it carries, the carbon it buries, the cell in a model, the state read from the past, and the centuries it takes.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个环路：整个循环、它下沉的寒冷起点、漫长的回程、教科书里画的传送带、它输送的热量、它封存的碳、模式中的单元、从过去读出的状态，以及它所花费的世纪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cold salty water sinking at the rim of the world and crawling back along the sea floor to rise elsewhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：世界边缘又冷又咸的水下沉，沿洋底爬行，再在别处升回海面。

branches.en: THE LOOP AND ITS START: the whole circuit, then the cold place where the descending limb begins.
branches.cn: 环路与起点：先是整个循环，然后是下沉支开始的寒冷海域。

branches.en: THE LONG WAY BACK: the return limb is why the whole loop is measured in centuries.
branches.cn: 漫长的回程：正是回流支决定了整个环路要以世纪来度量。

branches.en: PICTURE AND PIPES: a belt in the textbook, and a heating system in the climate.
branches.cn: 图像与管道：教科书里是传送带，气候系统里是供暖装置。

branches.en: WHAT IT CARRIES AND HOW IT IS MODELLED: carbon in the deep, and a single cell in a model.
branches.cn: 它载着什么、如何被模拟：深海中的碳，以及模式里的单个单元。

branches.en: READ IN MUD: past states of the loop reconstructed from sediment and ice.
branches.cn: 从泥里读出：由沉积物与冰重建出的环路过往状态。

intro.en: Thermohaline circulation is a two-word technical compound: one part built from Greek roots, one from a Latin root, and both recurrent in oceanography.
intro.cn: thermohaline circulation 是双词技术复合语：一部分由希腊词根构成，另一部分由拉丁词根构成，两者在海洋学中都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin circulus and circulatio supply the second word and its family: circle, circular, circulate and circuit all return to the same ring.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 circulus 与 circulatio 提供第二个词及其词族：circle、circular、circulate、circuit 都回到同一个圆圈。

items.example: Thermē is the first element of thermohaline.
items.exampleCN: thermē 是 thermohaline 的第一个成分。

items.example: Halinos contributes the salt half of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: halinos 提供了这个形容词中「盐」的那一半。

items.example: The ending makes a property adjective of the two roots.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把两个词根变成一个性质形容词。

items.example: Thermohaline contrasts drive the deep flow.
Circulus is the base of the whole circulation family.
items.exampleCN: circulus 是这一整族词的基干。

items.structure: circulare 'to move in a circle' + -tio (noun of action)

items.example: Circulation returns water to its starting point.
items.exampleCN: 环流把水送回它的起点。

items.example: Thermohaline circulation operates on a millennial scale.
items.exampleCN: 温盐环流以千年为尺度运转。

items.meaning: more than one such loop, as in other basins or models
items.meaningCN: 不止一个这样的环路，如其他海盆或模式中的
items.example: Models produce thermohaline circulations of different strengths.
items.exampleCN: 模式给出强度不同的温盐环流。

items.example: Heat circulates through the loop over centuries.
items.exampleCN: 热量在数百年间沿环路循环。

latinEntries.structure: circulare, circulo, circulavi, circulatus (v., first conjugation)

definition_zh: 校准；标定；刻度设定；（判断）校准
definition_en: the act or process of adjusting an instrument or scale so that its readings match a known standard
core_image: 一把标准尺贴在仪器刻度旁，把每一格推到正确的位置
scene: 这里指「校准」。 Before each experiment, the team runs a full calibration of the spectrometer against a known sample.
sceneCN: 这里 calibration 是「校准」（第 1 个义项：用已知标准调整仪器）；句意：每次实验前，团队都用已知样本对光谱仪做一次完整校准。场景要点：标准样本、仪器刻度盘、记录笔，每一格被对齐到已知值。

pos.zh: 校准；标定；刻度设定；（判断）校准

forms.label: 复数（多次校准或多项校准值）

senses.title: Adjusting an instrument to a standard
senses.titleCN: 仪器校准：把读数对齐已知标准
senses.definition: the act of checking and adjusting an instrument so that its readings agree with a known standard
senses.definitionCN: 检查并调整仪器，使其读数与已知标准一致的行为
senses.example: The calibration of the thermometer is repeated every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支温度计每年都要重新校准。
senses.why: Caliber named the bore of a gun. Calibrate first meant to measure that bore, then to fix any scale against a standard, and -ion names the process.
senses.whyCN: caliber 原本指炮管口径。calibrate 最初表示测定这个口径，后来表示让任何刻度对齐标准，-ion 命名这个过程。

senses.title: The state of being in adjustment
senses.definition: the condition of an instrument whose readings are known to be accurate
senses.definitionCN: 仪器读数已知准确的状态
senses.example: The gauge is out of calibration and must not be used.
senses.exampleCN: 这只仪表已经失准，不能使用。
senses.why: The result of the act is a state. English uses the same -ion noun for both the process and the standing condition it leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作的结果是一种状态。英语用同一个 -ion 名词既指过程，也指过程留下的持续状态。

senses.title: Setting the divisions of a scale
senses.titleCN: 刻度设定：决定每一格站在哪里
senses.definition: the marking or fixing of the divisions of a scale
senses.definitionCN: 标记或确定刻度上各分格的位置
senses.example: The calibration of the axis places zero at the freezing point.
senses.exampleCN: 这条轴的刻度设定把零点放在冰点。
senses.why: A scale is a row of marks. Calibration decides where each mark sits, so the noun also names the layout of the divisions rather than the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 刻度是一排标记。校准决定每个标记的位置，所以名词也指分格的排布，而不只是仪器。

senses.title: The reference relationship
senses.titleCN: 校准曲线：把信号与真值绑在一起
senses.definition: the established relationship between an instrument's signal and the true value
senses.definitionCN: 仪器信号与真实值之间建立起来的关系
senses.example: The concentration was read from the calibration curve.
senses.exampleCN: 浓度是从校准曲线上读出的。
senses.why: Once each mark is tied to a standard, the whole set of marks forms a curve or table. The noun is transferred from the act to the reference object produced by it.
senses.whyCN: 每个标记一旦绑定到一个标准，整套标记就构成一条曲线或一张表。名词于是从动作转到动作产生的参照物。

senses.title: Fine adjustment of a device
senses.titleCN: 设备调校：让参数回到工作区间
senses.definition: the tuning of a device or system so that it performs within its intended range
senses.definitionCN: 调整设备或系统，使其在预期范围内工作的过程
senses.example: Sensor calibration improved the camera's low-light performance.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器校准改善了相机的弱光表现。
senses.why: Modern devices have many parameters, not one scale. The word widens from a single needle to any setting that must be brought into line.
senses.whyCN: 现代设备有许多参数，而不只是一根指针。这个词从单根刻度扩展到任何需要被对齐的设置。

senses.title: Checking a model against data
senses.titleCN: 模型校准：让模型输出贴合观测
senses.definition: the process of testing and adjusting a model so that its output matches observations
senses.definitionCN: 检验并调整模型，使其输出与观测相符的过程
senses.example: Model calibration against field data reduced the error.
senses.exampleCN: 依据野外数据进行的模型校准降低了误差。
senses.why: A model is treated like an instrument: it produces readings, so it can be calibrated. The standard is now observed data rather than a physical gauge.
senses.whyCN: 模型被当作仪器：它会产生读数，因此可以被校准。此时的标准是观测数据，而不是物理量具。

senses.title: Calibration of confidence
senses.titleCN: 判断校准：自信程度与实际水平对得上吗
senses.definition: the accuracy with which a person's stated confidence matches actual performance
senses.definitionCN: 一个人表达的自信程度与其实际表现相符的准确度
senses.example: Forecasters studied the calibration of their confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员研究了自己信心的校准程度。
senses.why: This is the metaphor at its most abstract: confidence is a scale, and calibration measures whether its marks match reality.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个隐喻最抽象的用法：自信是一条刻度，校准衡量的是刻度是否与真实相符。

senses.title: Measuring a bore
senses.titleCN: 口径测定：最早的字面义
senses.definition: the original sense: determining the caliber, or inside diameter, of a gun barrel
senses.definitionCN: 最初的字面义：测定炮管口径，即内直径
senses.example: The calibration of the barrel decided which shot would fit.
senses.exampleCN: 炮管的口径测定决定了哪种炮弹能装进去。
senses.why: The oldest literal sense measured a bore. Later senses keep the shape of measuring against a fixed width, which is why the word can still mean 'set to a standard'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的字面义是测量孔径。后来的义项保留了“对着固定宽度测量”的形状，因此这个词仍能表示“对准标准”。

senses.title: Bringing standards into line
senses.titleCN: 标准对齐：让两套规范可比
senses.definition: the adjustment of standards, expectations, or policies so that they agree
senses.definitionCN: 调整标准、预期或政策，使其一致
senses.example: The two agencies agreed on a calibration of their safety standards.
senses.exampleCN: 两个机构就安全标准的对齐达成一致。
senses.why: Institutions also have scales. When separate standards must be made comparable, the instrument image is applied to rules and expectations.
senses.whyCN: 机构也有自己的刻度。当不同的标准需要变得可比时，仪器的意象就被用到规则和预期上。

intro.en: Calibration is a 19th-century derivative of calibrate, which was formed from caliber. The history of caliber itself is disputed, and the often-repeated Arabic-Greek chain is not established.
intro.cn: calibration 是 19 世纪由 calibrate 派生的名词，而 calibrate 又由 caliber 构成。caliber 本身的历史存在争议，常被转述的“阿拉伯—希腊”链条并未得到确证。

items.en: French calibre, recorded by the mid-16th century and perhaps in the late 15th, named the inside diameter of a gun barrel. English borrowed it as caliber in the 1580s.
items.cn: 法语 calibre 在 16 世纪中期有记录，也许可早到 15 世纪晚期，指炮管的内直径。英语在 16 世纪 80 年代把它借入为 caliber。

items.en: It is often said that calibre goes back to Arabic qalib 'a mold for casting'. Standard references repeat this with caution: Barnhart notes that Spanish and Italian forms appear too late to serve as intermediate links, and no documentary evidence supports the Arabic route.
items.cn: 常有人说 calibre 可追溯到阿拉伯语 qalib“铸造用的模具”。通行词源资料转述时都带保留：Barnhart 指出西班牙语和意大利语形式出现太晚，无法充当中间环节；也没有文献证据支持这条阿拉伯路径。

items.en: A still deeper link to Greek kalapous 'wooden shoe' is sometimes proposed. It is speculative and not accepted in standard etymological references, so it should be treated as uncertain rather than as fact.
items.cn: 偶尔还有人把它更往上联系到希腊语 kalapous“木鞋”。这属于推测，通行词源资料并不接受，因此应当作存疑处理，不能当作事实。

items.en: A rival 19th-century explanation derives calibre from Medieval Latin qua libra 'of what weight', from quis 'which' and libra 'balance'. This is also a hypothesis, not a settled fact.
items.cn: 19 世纪还有一种竞争性解释，认为 calibre 来自中古拉丁语 qua libra“按什么重量”，由 quis“哪一个”和 libra“天平”构成。这同样只是假说，并非定论。

items.en: Calibrate was formed in English in 1839 from caliber + -ate, meaning 'determine the caliber of'. By 1869 it also meant 'determine the relative value of the parts of an arbitrary scale'.
items.cn: calibrate 于 1839 年在英语中由 caliber + -ate 构成，意为“测定……的口径”。到 1869 年，它也指“确定任意刻度上各部分的相对数值”。

items.en: Calibration is recorded in 1854 as the noun of action of calibrate. The sense moved from measuring a bore to setting any scale, then to adjusting instruments, models, and even human confidence. The deeper origin of caliber remains uncertain.
items.cn: calibration 于 1854 年作为 calibrate 的行为名词出现。词义从测量口径扩展到设定任何刻度，再扩展到调整仪器、模型，甚至人的信心。caliber 的更早来源仍然存疑。

note.en: The look-alikes are the measuring and counting words that share the cal- shape; the near-meaning group contains words for adjustment and checking against a standard.
note.cn: 形近词是共享 cal- 外形的测量与计数词；近义词组则包含调整和对照标准检查类的词。

entries.definition: the inside diameter of a gun barrel, or the level of someone's ability. It is the noun from which calibrate was formed, not the act of adjusting.
entries.definitionCN: 炮管口径，或某人的能力水准。它是 calibrate 所由构成的名词，不是调整行为本身。

entries.definition: an instrument for measuring external or internal diameters. It is a measuring device, while calibration is the adjustment of a scale.
entries.definitionCN: 测量外径或内径的量具。它是测量工具，而 calibration 是对刻度的调整。

entries.definition: the act or result of computing with numbers. It shares the cal- beginning but comes from calculus 'pebble', not from caliber.
entries.definitionCN: 用数字计算的行为或结果。它共享 cal- 开头，但来自 calculus“石子”，并非来自 caliber。

entries.definition: to adjust an instrument against a standard. It is the verb; calibration adds -ion and names the act or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 对照标准调整仪器。它是动词；calibration 加 -ion，表示行为或结果。

entries.definition: a change made to fit a condition or purpose. It is broader than calibration and does not require a known standard.
entries.definitionCN: 为适应某条件或目的而作的改变。它比 calibration 宽泛，不要求有已知标准。

entries.definition: the adjustment of an instrument or system for best performance, especially by changing frequency. Calibration aims at accurate readings rather than optimal performance.
entries.definitionCN: 为获得最佳性能而调整仪器或系统，尤指改变频率。calibration 追求读数准确，而不是性能最优。

entries.definition: making things conform to one shared standard, often across an industry. It is a collective process; calibration is usually a local measurement adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 使事物符合一个共同标准，常跨行业进行。它是集体过程；calibration 通常是局部的测量调整。

entries.definition: the act of checking that something is true or accurate. It tests the reading but does not necessarily adjust the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 检查某事物是否真实或准确的行为。它检验读数，但未必调整仪器。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real gun-bore origin, the real suffix and the real laboratory collocations of calibration.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的炮口径来源、真实的后缀，以及 calibration 真实的实验室搭配。

normal.en: caliber = the bore of a gun. Calibration began as measuring that fixed width, then became setting any scale to a standard.
normal.cn: caliber 就是炮管口径。calibration 从测量这个固定宽度开始，后来变成把任何刻度对准标准。

normal.en: calibrate + -ion: the verb names the adjusting, and the noun names the act or the state it produces.
normal.cn: calibrate + -ion：动词命名调整动作，名词命名行为或它产生的状态。

normal.en: Out of calibration is the standard warning that an instrument's readings can no longer be trusted.
normal.cn: out of calibration 是标准警示语：仪器的读数不再可信。

normal.en: A calibration curve is the visible result of calibration: a line tying signal to true value.
normal.cn: calibration curve 是校准的可视结果：一条把信号与真值绑在一起的线。

normal.en: Calibration and calculation look alike but have different roots: caliber is a bore, calculus is a pebble.
normal.cn: calibration 与 calculation 形似，但词根不同：caliber 是口径，calculus 是石子。

abstract.en: Picture a standard ruler laid beside a dial: every mark on the dial is pushed until it lines up.
abstract.cn: 想象一把标准尺贴在刻度盘旁：盘上的每个标记都被推到对齐的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with a known weight on one side: the needle is moved until it reads that weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤的一边放着已知重量的砝码：指针被调到能读出这个重量。

abstract.en: Picture a metronome set to 100 beats: the setting is not the music, but it makes the music trustworthy.
abstract.cn: 想象把节拍器设到每分钟 100 拍：这个设定不是音乐，却让音乐变得可信。

examples.en: The laboratory keeps a log of every calibration performed on its balances.
examples.cn: 实验室为天平所做的每一次校准都保留记录。

examples.en: Without regular calibration, the sensor's readings drift away from the true value.
examples.cn: 如果不定期校准，传感器的读数就会偏离真实值。

examples.en: The forecasters measured the calibration of their confidence over a full year.
examples.cn: 预报员用整整一年时间测量自己信心的校准程度。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卡里布瑞申”——卡（ca）里（li）布（bra）瑞（tion），用卡尺卡住标准布一量，刻度就准了 → calibration 校准

root: 英语 caliber/calibre“炮口径”（16 世纪经法语 calibre 借入），calibrate“测定口径、校准”+ -ion；calibre 更深来源存疑：阿拉伯 qalib“模具”说缺乏证据，另有中古拉丁 qua libra“按何重量”说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all repeat one gesture: a reading is brought into line with a fixed reference, whether the scale belongs to an instrument, a model, a standard, or a person's confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都在重复同一个动作：让读数与一个固定参照对齐——无论这条刻度属于仪器、模型、标准，还是人的信心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a standard laid against a scale, with every mark pushed into line.
core.cn: 核心意象：把标准贴到刻度上，把每个标记推到对齐的位置。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: the adjustment and the trustworthy condition it leaves behind are the same noun.
branches.cn: 行为与状态：调整动作和它留下的可信状态，由同一个名词表示。

branches.en: THE SCALE ITSELF: fixing where the divisions sit produces the reference curve used for later readings.
branches.cn: 刻度本身：确定分格的位置，就产生了供后续读数使用的参照曲线。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND STANDARDS: device parameters and institutional rules are both brought into line.
branches.cn: 系统与标准：设备参数和机构规则，都被调到一致。

branches.en: MODELS AND MINDS: a model's output and a person's confidence can both be checked against reality.
branches.cn: 模型与心智：模型的输出和人的信心，都可以对照现实来检验。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL BORE: the oldest sense measured a gun barrel, and its shape survives in every later use.
branches.cn: 最初的口径：最古老的义项测量炮管，这个形状留在后来每一种用法里。

intro.en: Calibration is built from an English verb and a Latin suffix: calibrate + -ion. The productive step is -ion; the base calibr- is frozen inside caliber, whose own origin is disputed.
intro.cn: calibration 由英语动词加拉丁后缀构成：calibrate + -ion。有能产性的一步是 -ion；词基 calibr- 凝固在 caliber 内部，而 caliber 本身的来源存在争议。

latinIntro.en: There is no certain Latin ancestor for calibr-. The two rival explanations are Arabic qalib 'mold' and Medieval Latin qua libra 'of what weight'. The Latin side of the second hypothesis is listed below; it is a hypothesis, not an established root.
latinIntro.cn: calibr- 没有确证的拉丁祖先。两种竞争性解释是阿拉伯语 qalib“模具”和中古拉丁语 qua libra“按什么重量”。下面列出第二种假说中的拉丁成分；它只是假说，不是已确立的词根。

items.meaning: the act or result of calibrating
items.meaningCN: 校准；标定（-ion 表示行为）
items.example: The calibration of the instrument is complete.

items.meaning: to determine a caliber; to adjust a scale against a standard
items.meaningCN: 测定口径；校准（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: They calibrated the sensor before the test.
items.exampleCN: 测试前他们对传感器做了校准。

items.meaning: the inside diameter of a barrel; degree of quality
items.example: The rifle is of a small caliber.

items.meaning: same as caliber; also used figuratively for quality
items.meaningCN: caliber 的英式拼写；也用于比喻“水准”
items.example: The committee is looking for someone of her calibre.
items.exampleCN: 委员会正在找像她这种水准的人。

items.structure: probably from caliber, with a variant ending
items.meaningCN: 卡尺；测径器（可能由 caliber 变体而来）
items.example: Use the caliper to measure the pipe's diameter.
items.exampleCN: 用卡尺测量管子的直径。

items.meaningCN: 重新校准（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The machine recalibrates itself after each restart.
items.exampleCN: 每次重启后机器都会自动重新校准。

items.meaningCN: 重新校准（再次进行的校准）
items.example: A recalibration was needed after the move.
items.exampleCN: 搬动之后需要重新校准。

items.meaning: a device or person that calibrates
items.meaningCN: 校准器；校准员（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The calibrator generates a known signal.
items.exampleCN: 校准器会生成一个已知信号。

items.meaningCN: 已校准的；标定过的（-ed 构成分词形容词）
items.example: All calibrated instruments are stored separately.
items.exampleCN: 所有已校准的仪器都单独存放。

items.meaning: of a smaller caliber than the standard
items.meaningCN: 次口径的；小于标准口径的（sub- 表示“低于”）
items.example: The training round uses a subcaliber insert.
items.exampleCN: 训练弹使用一个次口径内衬。

latinEntries.structure: libra (Latin noun: balance, pair of scales; pound)
latinEntries.meaning: a balance or unit of weight; the weight element in the rival qua libra hypothesis
latinEntries.meaningCN: 天平；重量单位；竞争性 qua libra 假说中的“重量”成分

latinEntries.meaning: 'of what weight'; Mahn's 19th-century alternative source for caliber, not proven
latinEntries.meaningCN: “按什么重量”；Mahn 在 19 世纪提出的 caliber 替代来源，未获确证

latinEntries.meaning: a standard measure; related measuring vocabulary, but not the source of caliber
latinEntries.meaningCN: 标准量度；属于测量词汇的对照项，但不是 caliber 的来源

definition_zh: 惊骇的；吓呆的
definition_en: struck with shock, horror, or amazement
core_image: 血一下子凉透：惊吓从脚底窜上头顶
scene: 拆开信封，账单上的数字让他僵在原地。 He stood aghast at the sum on the final bill.
sceneCN: 这里 aghast 是「惊骇的」（第 1 个义项：被吓到失语僵立）；句意是看到最终账单上的金额，他惊得僵在原地。

pos.zh: 惊骇的；吓呆的（表语用法）

derivatives.zh: 同源日耳曼词 gast 的一支，义为「鬼魂」
ghost 同族形容词，义为「可怕的；苍白的」
aghast 加后缀 -ly（旧式罕用），义为「惊骇地」

senses.title: Struck with shock or horror
senses.definition: filled with sudden shock or terror, often shown by a frozen stare
senses.definitionCN: 充满突如其来的震惊或恐惧，常表现为僵住的凝视
senses.example: He stood aghast at the sum on the final bill.
senses.exampleCN: 看到最终账单上的金额，他惊得僵在原地。
senses.why: The Old English gast meant spirit or breath; to be aghast was to have the breath frightened out of you.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gast 意为「气息、灵魂」；aghast 的本义就是「被吓得魂飞魄散、气息全无」。

senses.title: Filled with horror at something seen as wrong
senses.titleCN: 对（不义之事）深感震惊的
senses.definition: shocked by something considered outrageous or unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 对被视为恶劣或不可接受之事感到震惊
senses.example: Readers were aghast that the prize went to a plagiarist.
senses.exampleCN: 奖项颁给了剽窃者，读者们惊骇不已。
senses.why: Horror at danger widened to moral shock: the same frozen breath meets a villain as a ghost.
senses.whyCN: 对危险的恐惧扩大为道义上的震惊：面对恶行与面对鬼魂，同样吓得倒抽冷气。

intro.en: From the past participle of agasten (to frighten), built on Old English gāst (spirit, ghost).
intro.cn: 源自动词 agasten「吓唬」的过去分词，建立在古英语 gāst（灵魂、鬼魂）之上。

items.en: The root *gheys- (to be excited, frightened) underlies gast and ghost.
items.cn: 一般认为词根 *gheys-（激动、惊惧）是 gast 与 ghost 的远源。

items.en: gāst meant breath, spirit, ghost; the verb agāstan meant to terrify.
items.cn: 古英语 gāst 意为「气息、灵魂、鬼魂」，动词 agāstan 意为「使恐惧」。

items.en: agast served as the past participle: frightened out of one's wits.
items.cn: 中古英语 agast 用作过去分词：「被吓得魂不附体」。

items.en: Spelling settled as aghast under the influence of ghost.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪拼写受 ghost 影响定型为 aghast。

items.en: Now almost purely predicative: stand aghast, be aghast at.
items.cn: 如今几乎只作表语：stand aghast、be aghast at。

note.en: Aghast names the frozen face of horror; appalled adds moral outrage, horrified adds fear.
note.cn: aghast 刻画惊骇时僵住的脸；appalled 多一层道义愤怒，horrified 多一层恐惧。

entries.definition: the spirit of a dead person
entries.definitionCN: 鬼魂——同源词，aghast 的吓人源头

entries.definition: frightful, dreadful
entries.definitionCN: 可怕的；苍白的——同族形容词

entries.definition: with the mouth wide open
entries.definitionCN: 目瞪口呆地——同为 a- 系状态词，情绪相邻

entries.definition: aghast is standard; aghastly is archaic
entries.definitionCN: aghast 是标准形；aghastly 已成古旧用法

entries.definition: shocked and disgusted
entries.definitionCN: 惊骇且愤慨的

entries.definition: filled with horror
entries.definitionCN: 惊恐的

entries.definition: struck speechless by shock
entries.definitionCN: 惊得说不出话的——与「气息被吓跑」意象呼应

entries.definition: calm, not disturbed
entries.definitionCN: 镇定的——aghast 的反面

normalIntro.en: See ghost inside the word: aghast means scared as if by a ghost.
normalIntro.cn: 在词里看见 ghost：aghast 就是被吓得见了鬼一般。

normal.en: a + ghast: the ghost has scared your breath away
normal.cn: a+ghast：鬼把你的气都吓没了

normal.en: stand aghast is the anchor collocation
normal.cn: stand aghast 是锚定搭配：惊得呆立

normal.en: aghast at the price, at the news, at the mess
normal.cn: aghast at 常接价格、消息、烂摊子

normal.en: ghost, ghastly, aghast: one frightening family
normal.cn: ghost、ghastly、aghast 同属「惊吓」家族

normal.en: aghast is for the face, agape is for the mouth
normal.cn: aghast 写脸上之惊，agape 写嘴上之张

abstract.en: A face draining white as a door creaks open
abstract.cn: 房门吱呀一响，一张脸瞬间血色尽失

abstract.en: Breath hanging in cold air, stopped mid-cloud
abstract.cn: 呵出的白气凝在半空，呼吸骤停

abstract.en: A juror frozen between verdict slips
abstract.cn: 陪审员捏着两页裁定书，僵在原地

examples.en: The court's verdict left the accused's family aghast.
examples.cn: 法庭判决让被告家人惊骇不已。

examples.en: Neighbours stood aghast as the crane toppled across the street.
examples.cn: 吊车横倒在街对面，邻居们看得目瞪口呆。

examples.en: She was aghast at how quickly the ancient carvings had been defaced.
examples.cn: 古代石刻竟被破坏得如此之快，她深感震惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额·嘎斯特」——见到 ghost（鬼），吓得倒抽一口冷气「嘎」的一声。谐音仅助记，并非词源。

root: 古英语 gāst「灵魂、气息」（一般认为出自印欧词根 *gheys-「激动、惊惧」，与 ghost 同源）派生动词 agasten「吓唬」，其过去分词 agast 经拼写演变定为 aghast；本义「气息被吓跑」，即「惊骇失色」。

sensesIntro.en: One frightened breath serves both the shock of danger and the shock of outrage.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次被吓住的呼吸，既回应危险，也回应不义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: breath stopped by sudden horror
core.cn: 核心意象：被突如其来的惊骇止住的呼吸

branches.en: terror that freezes the body
branches.cn: 令身体僵住的恐惧

branches.en: breath knocked out by what is seen
branches.cn: 被眼前之事夺走的呼吸

branches.en: horror at a moral wrong
branches.cn: 对不义之事的震惊

branches.en: public dismay at scandal
branches.cn: 对丑闻的公愤

branches.en: words failing the frightened
branches.cn: 吓坏了的人说不出话

intro.en: The word is a fossilized past participle: a- (intensive) plus gast, the root of ghost.
intro.cn: 该词是石化的过去分词：加强前缀 a- 加词根 gast（ghost 的本源）。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestry; Latin expresses horror through its own roots.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语用自有词根表达「惊骇」。

derivatives.zh: 可怕的；惨白的（同族形容词）

definition_zh: 凭此；借此；通过…方式
definition_en: by which; used to introduce the means or mechanism by which something is done
core_image: 一根绳子系在两岸，人正是抓着它过河
scene: 村里定下一条规矩：每户每年出一个人去修渠。 The village agreed on a rule whereby each household sends one worker to repair the channel each year.
sceneCN: 这里指这条规矩所规定的机制（第 1 个义项：凭此、借此引出实现方式）；句意为村里定下一条规矩，凭它每户每年派一人修渠。

pos.zh: 凭此；借此；通过…方式（关系副词，相当于「凭这个」）

derivatives.zh: 在哪里；在…之处（构词成分）
借此；由此（there + by 的同构复合词）
然而；鉴于（where + as 同构）

senses.title: The mechanism in a rule
senses.definition: used to introduce the mechanism that a rule or system sets up
senses.definitionCN: 引出某条规则或制度所设立的运作机制
senses.example: They agreed on a system whereby each member reports twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 他们商定了一种制度，凭它每位成员每年报告两次。
senses.why: Where points at the arrangement and by names the means, so the compound asks the reader to look inside the thing just mentioned for its workings.
senses.whyCN: where 指向那个安排，by 指出手段，因此这个复合词让读者到刚提到的事物内部去看它如何运转。

senses.title: The method in a process
senses.definition: used to name the method by which a process is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 引出完成某一过程所采用的方法
senses.example: They describe a process whereby waste is turned into fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们描述了一种过程，借此把废弃物变成燃料。
senses.why: The relative adverb attaches the method to the noun it follows, so the method is presented as belonging to the process itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个关系副词把方法挂在前面的名词上，因此方法被呈现为过程自身的一部分。

senses.title: The formula in a contract
senses.titleCN: 合同条款里的计算公式
senses.definition: used in legal drafting to introduce a formula or condition
senses.definitionCN: 法律起草中引出某一计算公式或条件
senses.example: The clause sets a formula whereby rent rises with inflation.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款订出一个公式，据此租金随通胀上调。
senses.why: Contracts must tie an obligation to a precise route, and whereby is the standard hinge for that route.
senses.whyCN: 合同必须把义务拴在一条精确的路线上，而 whereby 就是那条路线的标准铰链。

senses.title: The means to a result
senses.definition: used to show the means by which a result is produced
senses.definitionCN: 表明产生某一结果所凭的手段
senses.example: The valve opens, whereby pressure is released.
senses.exampleCN: 阀门打开，压力借此释放。
senses.why: Here the means and the result touch: opening the valve is the route by which the release happens.
senses.whyCN: 这里手段与结果相接：打开阀门正是压力得以释放的那条路。

senses.title: The channel for delivery
senses.titleCN: 资金或信息传递的渠道
senses.definition: used of a channel through which something reaches its destination
senses.definitionCN: 指某物抵达目的地所经的渠道
senses.example: They set up an arrangement whereby funds reach the villages directly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们做出一种安排，凭此资金直接到达各村。
senses.why: A channel is a by-route in space, which is why the compound suits money, goods and information.
senses.whyCN: 渠道是空间中的「经由之路」，所以这个复合词适用于资金、货物与信息。

senses.title: The tool for a task
senses.definition: used to name an instrument that makes a task possible
senses.definitionCN: 引出使某项任务得以完成的工具
senses.example: They designed a tool whereby the parts can be checked in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们设计了一种工具，借它几秒钟就能检查这些零件。
senses.why: An instrument is the most concrete kind of by, so the word naturally introduces devices as well as procedures.
senses.whyCN: 工具是「凭借」最具体的一种，因此这个词既能引出程序，也能引出器具。

senses.title: The relation between quantities
senses.definition: used in definitions to state the relation by which one quantity depends on another
senses.definitionCN: 在定义中陈述一个量依赖另一个量所凭的关系
senses.example: It is a relation whereby one quantity depends on another.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一种关系，凭它一个量取决于另一个量。
senses.why: Mathematics defines by relations, and the compound names the link that makes the definition work.
senses.whyCN: 数学靠关系作定义，这个复合词命名了使定义成立的那条联系。

senses.title: The act that creates a legal status
senses.definition: used in legal narrative for an act by which a status or liability arises
senses.definitionCN: 法律叙述中指产生某种地位或责任的举动
senses.example: He signed the deed, whereby he became responsible for the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 他签署了这份契据，据此他对该债务负责。
senses.why: In law an act can create an obligation, and the word marks the exact step where the status changes.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上，一个行为可以产生一项义务，这个词标出地位改变的那一步。

intro.en: Whereby is an English compound of where and by, first recorded in the thirteenth century. It is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed; the Latin qua and per quae are counterparts only.
intro.cn: whereby 是 where 与 by 的英语复合词，最早见于十三世纪。它属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条；拉丁语 qua 与 per quae 只是对应说法。

items.en: Hwær is the place word behind where, used both to ask and to relate.
items.cn: hwær 是 where 背后的处所词，既用于提问也用于关联。

items.en: Bi means near or by means of, and English by keeps both the place sense and the instrumental one.
items.cn: bi 意为在近旁、凭借，英语 by 既保留处所义，也保留工具义。

items.en: Wher-bi appears in early Middle English with the sense by which, tying a means to the noun before it.
items.cn: wher-bi 见于中古英语早期，义为「凭此」，把手段拴在前面的名词上。

items.en: Drafters of statutes and contracts adopt the word because it can pin an obligation to an exact route.
items.cn: 法条与合同的起草者采用这个词，因为它能把义务钉在一条精确的路线上。

items.en: Modern English keeps whereby mostly in formal, legal and technical prose; ordinary speech prefers by which or where.
items.cn: 现代英语主要在正式、法律与技术文字中保留 whereby；日常口语更爱用 by which 或 where。

note.en: The first group shares the where plus preposition pattern. The second group names the by-route in plainer words, which modern speech prefers.
note.cn: 第一组共享 where + 前置词的构词模式。第二组用更朴素的词说出「经由之路」，现代口语更偏爱它们。

entries.definition: In or at which place; the word the compound is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 在何处；复合词赖以构成的那个词。

entries.definition: By that means, pointing back instead of setting up a relative clause.
entries.definitionCN: 借此、由此，回指前文，而不是引导关系从句。

entries.definition: In which, pointing inside an arrangement rather than to its means.
entries.definitionCN: 在其中，指向安排内部，而非指向手段。

entries.definition: After which, immediately following an event.
entries.definitionCN: 于是、随即，紧接某事件之后。

entries.definition: In contrast, or in legal recitals, seeing that.
entries.definitionCN: 然而；在法律序言中作「鉴于」。

entries.definition: The plain relative phrase that whereby replaces.
entries.definitionCN: whereby 所替代的朴素关系短语。

entries.definition: Naming a channel rather than a tool.
entries.definitionCN: 指渠道而非工具。

entries.definition: An explicit statement of instrumentality.
entries.definitionCN: 明确说出「凭借手段」。

entries.definition: Used of a rule or arrangement rather than a method.
entries.definitionCN: 用于规则或安排，而非方法。

entries.definition: Introduces a purpose or result rather than a mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 引出目的或结果，而不是机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real where plus by compound, the contract formula and the plain phrase by which.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 where + by 复合结构、合同公式，以及朴素说法 by which。

normal.en: Where plus by is literally at which by, the junction of a place and a means.
normal.cn: where 加 by 字面上是「在那一处凭借」，是地点与手段的接合处。

normal.en: Contracts love whereby because an obligation needs a route, not a slogan.
normal.cn: 合同喜欢 whereby，因为义务需要的是一条路线，而不是一句口号。

normal.en: In every day speech people say by which; whereby belongs to the written register.
normal.cn: 日常说话人们用 by which；whereby 属于书面语域。

normal.en: Thereby points back, whereby points forward to the mechanism that follows.
normal.cn: thereby 回指前文，whereby 则指向后面要说明的机制。

normal.en: A valve opening whereby pressure escapes is mechanism and result in one breath.
normal.cn: 「阀门打开，压力借此释放」一口气说出了机制与结果。

abstract.en: A rope across a river is not the crossing, but it is the whereby of the crossing.
abstract.cn: 横在河上的绳子不是渡河本身，但它是渡河的「凭此」。

abstract.en: Every institution is a whereby written down and forgotten.
abstract.cn: 每一项制度都是被写下来、然后被遗忘的「凭此」。

abstract.en: The word asks one question only: through what does this happen?
abstract.cn: 这个词只问一个问题：这件事经由什么发生？

examples.en: They created a channel whereby complaints reach the manager directly.
examples.cn: 他们建立了一条渠道，凭此投诉能直达经理。

examples.en: The treaty established a procedure whereby disputes are settled by arbitration.
examples.cn: 该条约确立了一套程序，据此争端通过仲裁解决。

examples.en: There is no known mechanism whereby the signal could cross the barrier.
examples.cn: 目前没有已知的机制能让该信号越过这道屏障。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「威尔拜」，where 是「那里」，by 是「凭借」：在那里凭借它，就是凭此

root: 英语复合词 where（古英语 hwær「在哪里」）+ by（古英语 bī「在旁、凭借」），十三世纪合为一词，义为「凭此」，作关系副词把手段拴在其前的名词上。属日耳曼语，无拉丁同族词，latinEntries 留空。现代英语主要保留于法律、合同与技术文字。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer through what: the mechanism of a rule, the method of a process, the formula in a contract, the route to a result, the channel of delivery, the tool for a task, the relation between quantities, and the act that creates a legal status.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答「经由什么」：规则的机制、过程的方法、合同里的公式、通往结果的路、传递的渠道、任务的工具、量之间的关系，以及产生法律地位的举动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope stretched across a river, the thing people actually hold on to.
core.cn: 核心意象：横跨河面的一根绳子，正是人实际抓住的东西。

branches.en: THE RULE: the working mechanism built into a system.
branches.cn: 规则：制度内部自带的运作机制。

branches.en: THE METHOD AND TOOL: how a process runs, and the instrument that makes a task possible.
branches.cn: 方法与工具：过程如何运转，以及使任务可行的器具。

branches.en: THE FORMULA: the precise route a clause writes into an obligation.
branches.cn: 公式：条款写进义务的那条精确路线。

branches.en: THE WAY THROUGH: the means that produces a result, and the channel that delivers it.
branches.cn: 经由之路：产生结果的手段，以及把结果送达的渠道。

branches.en: THE LINK AND THE ACT: a relation between quantities, and a step that changes a legal status.
branches.cn: 联系与举动：量之间的关系，以及改变法律地位的一步。

intro.en: Whereby is a compound of where and by rather than a prefixed word. English reuses where with prepositions in wherein, whereupon and whereas, and with there in thereby.
intro.cn: whereby 是 where 与 by 的复合词，不是加前缀的词。英语把 where 与前置词组成 wherein、whereupon、whereas，并与 there 组成 thereby。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed; qua and per quae express the same link in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条；拉丁语 qua 与 per quae 表达同一种联系。

definition_en: to bend low or shrink back in fear

senses.title: Shrink in fear
senses.definition: to make the body small because of fear
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧把身体缩起来
senses.example: The children cowered as the bomb fell.

senses.title: Submit timidly

senses.definitionCN: 怯懦地向人屈服

definition_zh: 典礼的；仪式上使用的；拘泥礼节的
definition_en: relating to a ceremony, used in a ceremony, or marked by excessive formality
core_image: 宫门前的石阶上铺着长毯，侍卫换上镶金边的礼服
scene: 宫门前的石阶上铺着长毯，侍卫换上镶金边的礼服。 The mayor's ceremonial role is to cut the ribbon, not to set the budget.
sceneCN: 这里 ceremonial 指「典礼的、仪式上使用的」（第 1 个义项：属于典礼场合的）；句意为市长这一职位的礼仪性职责是剪彩，而非决定预算。可辨识物件：石阶、长毯、礼服、金边、剪刀。

senses.title: Belonging to a ceremony
senses.definition: connected with a formal ceremony rather than with ordinary use
senses.definitionCN: 与正式典礼相关，而非与日常使用相关
senses.example: The mayor's ceremonial role is to cut the ribbon, not to set the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 市长这一职位的礼仪性职责是剪彩，而非决定预算。
senses.why: the adjective is built from the noun of worship, so it points at the occasion rather than the function.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由表礼拜的名词构成，因此指向场合而非功能。

senses.title: Used or worn in a ceremony
senses.titleCN: 典礼上使用的（服饰与器物）
senses.definition: describing robes, swords, plates or seats reserved for formal rites
senses.definitionCN: 描述专供正式仪式使用的袍服、剑、器皿或座位
senses.example: The ceremonial sword is kept in a glass case.
senses.exampleCN: 礼仪用剑被保存在玻璃柜中。
senses.why: objects become ceremonial when their use is fixed to one kind of occasion.
senses.whyCN: 当器物的用途被固定于某类场合，它就成了礼仪性的。

senses.title: Stiffly polite in manner
senses.definition: describing behaviour that is more formal than the situation requires
senses.definitionCN: 描述比场合所需更正式的行为
senses.example: Their ceremonial politeness made the small room feel colder.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拘礼的客气让这间小屋显得更冷。
senses.why: the same word can criticize formality when the rite has no real occasion.
senses.whyCN: 当仪式并无真正场合时，同一个词就能批评这种形式化。

senses.title: Official and state ritual
senses.definition: belonging to the formal duties of a state or its officers
senses.definitionCN: 属于国家或其官员的正式职责
senses.example: The president's ceremonial duties include receiving ambassadors.
senses.exampleCN: 总统的礼仪性职责包括接见大使。
senses.why: states separate the power to decide from the ceremony of representing.
senses.whyCN: 国家把决策之权与代表性的礼仪分开。

senses.title: Belonging to religious rite
senses.definition: describing the prescribed forms of worship and its objects
senses.definitionCN: 描述礼拜的规定形式及其器物
senses.example: The ceremonial washing precedes every offering.
senses.exampleCN: 每次献祭之前都要行礼仪性的洗涤。
senses.why: this is the oldest layer, where ceremony meant the awe of worship.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层，当时 ceremony 指礼拜的敬畏。

senses.title: Symbolic without real power
senses.titleCN: 仅有象征意义而无实权的
senses.definition: describing a title or body that performs the forms of authority but does not decide
senses.definitionCN: 描述只履行权威形式却不作决定的头衔或机构
senses.example: The council is largely ceremonial under the new charter.
senses.exampleCN: 根据新宪章，这个议事会基本只是礼仪性的。
senses.why: when power moves elsewhere, the old forms remain as ceremony without content.
senses.whyCN: 当权力转移，旧形式便作为无内容的仪式留存下来。

senses.title: Grand in scale and display
senses.definition: marked by elaborate display, uniform and staging
senses.definitionCN: 以繁复排场、制服与场面调度为特征
senses.example: The ceremonial arrival lasted longer than the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 礼仪性的抵达比会谈本身还长。
senses.why: display is how an occasion makes its importance visible to a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 排场是场合向人群展示重要性的方式。

senses.title: Performed for form rather than use
senses.titleCN: 仪式性动作而非实用的
senses.definition: done as a sign or form, without practical effect
senses.definitionCN: 作为标志或形式完成，没有实际效果
senses.example: The first cut was ceremonial; the machine did the real work.
senses.exampleCN: 第一刀只是仪式性的，真正干活的是机器。
senses.why: the word marks the line between acting out a role and doing the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出演角色与做实事之间的界线。

intro.en: Ceremonial comes from Late Latin caerimonialis 'belonging to worship', from caerimonia 'religious rite', a noun of uncertain and possibly Etruscan origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceremonial 来自晚期拉丁 caerimonialis「属于礼拜的」，而该词出自 caerimonia「宗教仪式」，后者来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caerimonia named worship and the awe around it. Source uncertain: no convincing Latin or Indo-European derivation is established, and an Etruscan origin is a common suggestion rather than a proof.
items.cn: caerimonia 指礼拜以及围绕它的敬畏。来源不确定：尚无令人信服的拉丁或印欧语派生来源，源自伊特鲁里亚语是常见推测而非证明。

items.en: The suffix -alis formed the adjective 'belonging to worship', used of books, vestments and gestures.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 构成形容词「属于礼拜的」，用于书籍、法衣与动作。

items.en: Old French ceremonial carried the adjective into English, where it first described church rites and their objects.
items.cn: 古法语 ceremonial 把这个形容词带入英语，最初描述教会礼仪及其器物。

items.en: Courts then borrowed the word for official duties that represent power without exercising it.
items.cn: 此后宫廷借用这个词，指代表权力却不行使权力的正式职责。

items.en: The critical sense 'merely symbolic' grew as constitutional states separated ceremony from decision.
items.cn: 随着宪政国家把礼仪与决策分离，批评性的「只是象征」义随之出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin and dates): the pre-Latin source of caerimonia is unsettled, and the first uses of the symbolic sense are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词源与年代）：caerimonia 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，象征义的最早用法也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same family that differ in meaning; group two holds words for roles and styles that are easily mixed up with this one.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中含义不同的形式；第二组是容易与之混淆的角色与风格词。

entries.definition: The event itself; ceremonial is what belongs to it or what it uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动本身；ceremonial 指属于它或它所使用的东西。

entries.definition: Describes a person or manner as stiffly polite; ceremonial can describe objects and roles.
entries.definitionCN: 描述人或举止拘礼；ceremonial 可描述器物与角色。

entries.definition: The adverb, used of performing an act as a rite rather than for use.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指把某动作当作仪式而非实用行为来完成。

entries.definition: Attachment to ritual forms for their own sake.
entries.definitionCN: 指为形式本身而依附礼仪。

entries.definition: Carrying meaning beyond the act; a ceremonial act is often symbolic, but not every symbol is a rite.
entries.definitionCN: 指承载动作之外的意义；礼仪性动作常是象征性的，但并非每个符号都是仪式。

entries.definition: Holding a title without its powers; it stresses the empty office, not the ritual display.
entries.definitionCN: 指只拥头衔而无实权；强调空衔，而非仪式排场。

entries.definition: Following set rules of style or procedure; ceremonial is narrower and ties form to a rite.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵循既定风格或程序规则；ceremonial 更窄，把形式绑在仪式上。

entries.definition: The ordered act; ceremonial describes what surrounds or belongs to such an act.
entries.definitionCN: 指有序的行为；ceremonial 描述围绕或属于这种行为的事物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ceremonial and ceremony share one Latin noun of worship; -alis made the adjective.
normal.cn: ceremonial 与 ceremony 共用同一个表礼拜的拉丁名词，-alis 构成形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: ceremonial role, ceremonial dress, ceremonial duties, ceremonial opening.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：礼仪性职责、礼服、礼仪性职责、剪彩仪式。

normal.en: A ceremonial head of state reigns and represents but does not govern.
normal.cn: 礼仪性国家元首在位并代表国家，但不执政。

normal.en: The family runs ceremony, ceremonial, ceremonious, ceremonially and ceremonialism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ceremony、ceremonial、ceremonious、ceremonially 与 ceremonialism。

normal.en: Keep ceremonial apart from ceremonious: objects and roles versus stiff politeness.
normal.cn: 要把 ceremonial 与 ceremonious 分开：前者指器物与角色，后者指拘谨的客气。

abstract.en: Picture a golden key that opens nothing but makes everyone stand up.
abstract.cn: 想象一把金钥匙，什么也打不开，却让所有人起立。

abstract.en: Picture a robe heavier than the body inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一件袍子，比穿它的人还重。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon cut long after the building is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象大楼早已完工，彩带却才被剪断。

examples.en: The ceremonial welcome included a band and a guard of honour.
examples.cn: 礼仪性的欢迎包括乐队与仪仗队。

examples.en: Her title is ceremonial; the real decisions are made elsewhere.
examples.cn: 她的头衔只是礼仪性的，真正的决定在别处做出。

examples.en: The vessel is ceremonial and never used for drinking.
examples.cn: 这件器皿是礼仪用的，从不用于饮水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ceremony（典礼）+ al（……的）」——典礼上的、礼仪性的

root: 晚期拉丁 caerimonialis「属于礼拜的」，出自 caerimonia「宗教仪式」；caerimonia 来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语。经法语进入英语作 ceremonial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one label: something is set aside for a formal occasion, and that setting-aside is then read as dress, politeness, state duty, worship, empty title, display and pure form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个标签展开：某物被划归正式场合专用，这种划归再依次被读作服饰、客套、国家职责、礼拜、空衔、排场与纯形式。

core.cn: 核心意象：一条铺在石阶上的长毯，标出一条不供日常通行的路。

branches.en: THE OCCASION: the adjective begins by pointing to the ceremony itself.
branches.cn: 场合：这个形容词先指向典礼本身。

branches.en: THINGS SET APART: a robe and a first cut are both removed from ordinary use.
branches.cn: 被划出之物：礼服与第一刀都被移出日常用途。

branches.en: POLITENESS AND SPECTACLE: too much formality can chill a room or fill a square.
branches.cn: 客套与排场：过多的形式既能冷却一室，也能填满广场。

branches.en: THRONE AND ALTAR: state and church both dress their authority in prescribed form.
branches.cn: 王座与祭坛：国家与教会都用规定形式给权威穿衣。

branches.en: THE EMPTY OFFICE: when decision moves away, the forms remain and the word turns critical.
branches.cn: 空衔：当决策移走，形式留下，这个词便带上批评。

intro.en: Ceremonial is a Late Latin adjective built from a noun of uncertain origin, and English later made nouns and adverbs from it.
intro.cn: ceremonial 是一个由来源不确定的名词构成的晚期拉丁形容词，英语后来又以它造出名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Caerimonia supplied the stem and -alis the relational ending; English added -ly, -ism and -ist to build the rest of the family.
latinIntro.cn: caerimonia 提供词干，-alis 提供关系词尾；英语又加 -ly、-ism 与 -ist 构成词族其余成员。

items.structure: caerimonia, caerimoniae (Latin noun, first declension; origin uncertain)
items.example: The noun named the awe before it named the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指敬畏，后指活动。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: The adjective covered books, robes and gestures.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词涵盖书籍、袍服与动作。

items.meaning: of a ceremony; the system of rites

items.exampleCN: 英语把它兼作形容词与名词。

items.example: The ground was ceremonially swept first.
The suffix turns the adjective into a tendency.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成一种倾向。

items.meaning: a person devoted to ritual form
items.example: The noun names a person rather than an event.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指人，不指活动。

items.example: The noun is the base the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 名词是形容词所描述的基础。

items.example: The -ous form points at people, not objects.
