definition_zh: 代谢的；新陈代谢的；与代谢速率、通路或代谢疾病相关的
definition_en: relating to metabolism, or to the rate, pathways and disorders of the body's chemical turnover
core_image: 一条环形流水线被画上刻度盘，盘上指针上下移动，旁边贴着「这条线的状态」的标签
scene: 这里指「代谢的」。 Metabolic rate falls at night, so the body burns less fuel while asleep.
sceneCN: 这里 metabolic 指「代谢速率的」（第 2 个义项：修饰速率，说明周转的快慢）；夜间速率下降，睡眠时消耗的燃料更少。图中可辨识物件：环形流水线、刻度盘、上下摆动的指针、状态标签。

pos.zh: 代谢的；新陈代谢的（多作定语，修饰 rate、pathway、disease 等）

senses.title: Of metabolism as a whole
senses.definition: relating to metabolism in general
senses.definitionCN: 与新陈代谢整体相关
senses.example: Metabolic processes keep the cell's chemistry in balance.
senses.exampleCN: 代谢过程使细胞的化学保持平衡。
senses.why: the -ic suffix turns the process into a relational adjective, so the word first means 'of metabolism'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ic 把过程变成关系形容词，因此这个词首先意为「代谢的」。

senses.title: The speed of the loop
senses.definition: describing the rate at which the body's turnover runs
senses.definitionCN: 描述身体周转运行的速率
senses.example: A higher metabolic rate lets a small mammal stay warm in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 较高的代谢率让小型哺乳动物在冬天保持体温。
senses.why: once physiologists measured the loop, the adjective attached to its speed, not only to its existence.
senses.whyCN: 当生理学家开始测定这条环路，这个形容词便附着在它的速度上，而不只是它的存在。

senses.title: A route inside the map
senses.definition: describing one route or step within the network of reactions
senses.definitionCN: 描述反应网络中的某条路线或某个步骤
senses.example: Glycolysis is a metabolic pathway shared by almost all cells.
senses.exampleCN: 糖酵解是几乎所有细胞共有的代谢通路。
senses.why: the loop is drawn as many routes, so the adjective also marks a single path through the map.
senses.whyCN: 这条环路被画成许多路线，因此这个形容词也标记地图中的单条路径。

senses.title: Disorder of the turnover
senses.definition: describing disease caused by a fault in metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 描述由代谢缺陷引起的疾病
senses.example: Phenylketonuria is a metabolic disease found at birth screening.
senses.exampleCN: 苯丙酮尿症是一种在新生儿筛查中发现的代谢病。
senses.why: when one route fails, the whole body feels it, so the adjective names a clinical class.
senses.whyCN: 当某条路线失灵，全身都会受影响，因此这个形容词命名一个临床类别。

senses.title: What the loop leaves behind
senses.titleCN: 代谢废物的：周转的残余
senses.definition: describing substances produced as by-products of metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 描述作为代谢副产物产生的物质
senses.example: The kidneys clear metabolic waste such as urea.
senses.exampleCN: 肾脏清除尿素等代谢废物。
senses.why: every route has leftovers, so the adjective also qualifies what must be removed rather than what is used.
senses.whyCN: 每条路线都有残余，因此这个形容词也限定必须被清走的东西，而不是被使用的东西。

senses.title: Of the enzymes that run it
senses.titleCN: 代谢酶的：驱动周转的催化者
senses.definition: describing the enzymes and controls that keep the routes running
senses.definitionCN: 描述维持路线运行的酶与调控
senses.example: Metabolic enzymes are often the target of drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 代谢酶常是药物的靶点。
senses.why: since the loop is run by catalysts, the adjective extends to the machinery that drives it.
senses.whyCN: 由于环路由催化剂驱动，这个形容词便延伸到驱动它的机器。

senses.title: Busy tissue
senses.definition: describing tissue or an organ with a high turnover, such as liver or muscle in exercise
senses.definitionCN: 描述周转旺盛的组织或器官，如肝脏或运动中的肌肉
senses.example: The liver is the most metabolically active organ per gram.
senses.exampleCN: 按每克计，肝脏是代谢最活跃的器官。
senses.why: high turnover is a visible property of a tissue, so the adjective can describe a state rather than a process.
senses.whyCN: 高周转是组织可见的属性，因此这个形容词可以描述一种状态，而非一个过程。

senses.title: The clustered clinical picture
senses.titleCN: 代谢综合征的：成组出现的临床征象
senses.definition: describing the cluster of obesity, high blood sugar, high lipids and hypertension
senses.definitionCN: 描述肥胖、高血糖、高血脂与高血压成组出现的情形
senses.example: Metabolic syndrome raises the risk of diabetes and heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 代谢综合征提高糖尿病与心脏病的风险。
senses.why: modern medicine grouped several signs under one name, so the adjective came to label that cluster.
senses.whyCN: 现代医学把若干征象归在一个名下，这个形容词便用来标记那一组。

intro.en: Metabolic is metabolism plus the relational suffix -ic, from Latin -icus and Greek -ikos. The base came from Greek metabolē 'a change'.
intro.cn: metabolic 是 metabolism 加关系后缀 -ic，后者出自拉丁 -icus 与希腊 -ikos；词基来自希腊 metabolē「变化」。

items.en: metabolē 'a change, a turning over' comes from meta- 'over' plus ballein 'to throw'; English metabolism was first a general word for change.
items.cn: metabolē「变化、翻转」由 meta-「越过」加 ballein「投掷」构成；英语 metabolism 最初泛指变化。

items.en: Greek -ikos formed adjectives of relation, and Latin took it as -icus; English keeps both as -ic.
items.cn: 希腊 -ikos 构成关系形容词，拉丁语吸收为 -icus；英语保留为 -ic。

items.en: The adjective appears in nineteenth-century physiology once metabolism was fixed as the body's chemical turnover; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 当 metabolism 被固定为体内化学周转后，该形容词于 19 世纪生理学文献中出现；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine produced metabolic disease, metabolic syndrome and metabolic rate as standard labels.
items.cn: 20 世纪医学产生了 metabolic disease、metabolic syndrome、metabolic rate 等标准标签。

items.en: Biochemistry in the same century mapped the routes and fixed metabolic pathway as a term.
items.cn: 同一世纪的生物化学绘出路线图，并固定了 metabolic pathway 这一术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): ballein has no agreed pre-Greek origin and the Indo-European forms behind it are reconstructions; the earliest citation of the adjective is also not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：ballein 在希腊语之前的来源无共识，其印欧形式属重构；该形容词的最早书证亦无确切记录。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same family or of a look-alike prefix; group two holds adjectives used in the same physiological sentences.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词或前缀形近词；第二组是出现在同一类生理学句子中的形容词。

entries.definition: The process itself. Metabolic qualifies a rate, route or disease, and cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；metabolic 只限定速率、路线或疾病，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: To act on a substance, as in 'the liver metabolizes the drug'. It names an action, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指对物质起作用，如「肝脏代谢该药」；命名动作，不是性质。

entries.definition: Cancer spread, from meta- plus stasis 'standing'. It shares meta- but not ballein, so it is not a metabolic relative.
entries.definitionCN: 指癌症转移，由 meta- 加 stasis「站立」构成；共享 meta-，但词根不是 ballein，故与 metabolic 不同族。

entries.definition: A product or input of metabolism. It is a countable molecule and never an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指代谢的产物或输入物；是可数分子，从不用作形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to catabolism, the breaking-down reactions. It is a narrower label than metabolic.
entries.definitionCN: 与分解代谢的拆解反应相关；比 metabolic 范围更窄。

entries.definition: Relating to anabolism, the building reactions that consume energy.
entries.definitionCN: 与消耗能量的合成反应相关。

entries.definition: Relating to the chemistry of living things generally; metabolic points specifically at the turnover.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生物体内的化学；metabolic 特指周转过程。

entries.definition: Describing energy or liveliness; it does not name the body's chemical loop.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能量或活力；不命名体内的化学环路。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: metabolism + -ic: the relational ending of metabolic, catabolic and anabolic.
normal.cn: metabolism + -ic：与 metabolic、catabolic、anabolic 相同的关系词尾。

normal.en: The family runs metabolism, metabolic, metabolize, metabolite, metabolically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 metabolism、metabolic、metabolize、metabolite、metabolically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: metabolic rate, metabolic pathway, metabolic disease, metabolic syndrome.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：代谢率、代谢通路、代谢病、代谢综合征。

normal.en: The pair is easy: metabolism is the loop, metabolic is the adjective of the loop.
normal.cn: 这组很好分：metabolism 是环路，metabolic 是环路的形容词。

normal.en: Exercise raises metabolic rate, and the liver is the most metabolically active organ by weight.
normal.cn: 运动会提高代谢率，而按重量计肝脏是代谢最活跃的器官。

abstract.en: Picture a dial on a conveyor loop, with a needle showing how fast it turns.
abstract.cn: 想象环形传送带上装一个表盘，指针显示它转得多快。

abstract.en: Picture a map where each route is one coloured line in a single network.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每条路线都是同一网络中的一条彩线。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger that records both what is spent and what is thrown away.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，既记录花费，也记录丢弃。

examples.en: Metabolic activity in the brain stays high even during sleep.
examples.cn: 睡眠中大脑的代谢活动依然很高。

examples.en: A metabolic disorder was found in the newborn screening.
examples.cn: 新生儿筛查中发现了一种代谢障碍。

examples.en: The drug blocks a metabolic pathway used by the parasite.
examples.cn: 该药阻断寄生虫使用的一条代谢通路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「代谢（metabolism）＋ic」——带代谢属性的 → 代谢的、代谢速率的

root: 希腊 metabolē「变化」（meta- + ballein「投掷」）→ metabolism + 拉丁 -icus / 希腊 -ikos → metabolic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one relational suffix: the whole loop, its speed, one route, its failures, its leftovers, its enzymes, a busy tissue, and a cluster of clinical signs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个表关系的后缀散开：整条环路、它的速度、单条路线、它的故障、它的残余、它的酶、活跃的组织，以及一组临床征象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial mounted on a turning loop, measuring how fast the loop runs.
core.cn: 核心意象：环形传送带上装着表盘，测量环路转得多快。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: the plainest reading, 'of metabolism'.
branches.cn: 归属：最朴素的义项，「代谢的」。

branches.en: SPEED: the dial reading, the rate of turnover.
branches.cn: 速度：表盘读数，即周转速率。

branches.en: ROUTES AND MACHINERY: a single pathway and the enzymes that run it.
branches.cn: 路线与机器：单条通路，以及驱动它的酶。

branches.en: FAILURE AND RESIDUE: disease when a route breaks, and waste that must be cleared.
branches.cn: 故障与残余：路线断裂时的疾病，以及必须清除的废物。

branches.en: STATE AND SYNDROME: a busy tissue, and several signs grouped under one label.
branches.cn: 状态与综合征：活跃的组织，以及归在一个标签下的若干征象。

intro.en: Metabolic is the Greek-derived noun metabolism plus the relational suffix -ic, from Latin -icus and Greek -ikos.
intro.cn: metabolic 是希腊来源名词 metabolism 加关系后缀 -ic，后者出自拉丁 -icus 与希腊 -ikos。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix series is Latin-based; the base is the Greek metabolē, and New Latin metabolismus is a Latinized spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀系列基于拉丁语；词基是希腊 metabolē，新拉丁语 metabolismus 只是拉丁化拼写。

items.example: Metabolic rate is measured at rest.
items.exampleCN: 代谢率在静息状态下测定。

items.meaning: a substance made or used in metabolism
items.example: The metabolite was excreted in urine.

items.exampleCN: 细胞代谢葡萄糖以获得能量。
分解代谢类激素升高血糖。
合成代谢通路需要 ATP。

items.example: The pathway is conserved in bacteria.

items.exampleCN: 代谢综合征以临床方式诊断。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to, of the nature of

definition_zh: 物理风化；岩石因机械力量破碎而成分不变的过程
definition_en: the breakdown of rock by mechanical forces such as frost, salt growth, pressure release or abrasion
core_image: 高山岩缝里的一层冰把两侧岩壁顶开，清晨一块碎石落在雪面上
scene: 高山上裸露的岩缝在夜里灌进雪水，天亮时冰把两侧岩壁撑开，碎石滚了一地，向导说 Physical weathering splits this granite without changing what it is made of.
sceneCN: 这里 physical weathering 指「岩石被机械力量弄碎而成分不变的过程」，取第 1 个义项（总称）；句意为物理风化把这花岗岩劈裂，却不改变它的成分。图中可辨识物件：岩缝、冰楔、碎石、雪面。

pos.zh: 物理风化、机械风化（不可数，地质学用语）

derivatives.zh: 风化的；表面被自然力磨损的

senses.title: Rock broken by force alone
senses.definition: the set of processes that break rock into pieces without altering its mineral composition
senses.definitionCN: 把岩石弄碎而不改变其矿物成分的一整套过程
senses.example: Physical weathering leaves the same minerals behind, only in smaller pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 物理风化留下的还是同样的矿物，只是碎成了小块。
senses.why: Physical here means mechanical: the rock loses shape and coherence, not its chemical identity.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 physical 指机械方式：岩石失去的是形状与整体性，而不是化学身份。

senses.title: Frost wedging
senses.definition: water entering cracks, freezing, expanding and prising the rock apart, then repeating
senses.definitionCN: 水进入裂缝后结冰膨胀，把岩石撑开，如此反复
senses.example: Frost wedging is the leading form of physical weathering in alpine valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 冻融作用是高寒河谷里物理风化的主要形式。
senses.why: Water expands when it freezes, so a filled crack pushes outward with force far beyond what the rock can bear.
senses.whyCN: 水结冰时体积膨胀，因此灌满的裂缝向外顶出的力量远超岩石的承受能力。

senses.title: Salt crystallisation
senses.definition: salts growing in pores as water evaporates, pushing the grain boundaries apart
senses.definitionCN: 水分蒸发后盐在孔隙中结晶，把颗粒边界顶开
senses.example: Salt crystallisation flakes the sandstone of desert cliffs.
senses.exampleCN: 盐结晶使沙漠崖壁的砂岩层层剥落。
senses.why: Growing crystals exert pressure against the pore walls, and repeated wetting and drying multiplies the damage.
senses.whyCN: 生长的晶体对孔隙壁施加压力，反复的干湿交替又把这破坏成倍放大。

senses.title: Unloading and exfoliation
senses.definition: rock expanding and sheeting off in slabs once the weight above it is removed
senses.definitionCN: 上方压力被移除后，岩石膨胀并按板状层层剥离
senses.example: Unloading produced the curved sheets of granite on the dome.
senses.exampleCN: 卸荷作用使花岗岩穹丘上出现弯曲的剥落板片。
senses.why: Deep rock is compressed; when erosion uncovers it, stored strain is released and the surface peels away.
senses.whyCN: 深处的岩石原本受压，侵蚀把它暴露后，储存的应变释放出来，表层便成片剥落。

senses.title: Abrasion and impact
senses.definition: sand, gravel or ice grinding and hammering the rock surface away
senses.definitionCN: 沙、砾石或冰对岩石表面的磨擦与撞击消耗
senses.example: Wind abrasion is physical weathering that polishes as well as cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 风蚀磨蚀是一种既切割又打磨的物理风化。
senses.why: Moving sediment carries kinetic energy, so repeated collisions chip the rock grain by grain.
senses.whyCN: 移动的泥沙携带动能，反复撞击便一粒一粒地把岩石削掉。

senses.title: Thermal expansion and contraction
senses.definition: repeated heating and cooling cracking the surface through differential expansion
senses.definitionCN: 反复加热与冷却因膨胀差异而使表层开裂
senses.example: Thermal expansion splits dark stones in the desert faster than pale ones.
senses.exampleCN: 在沙漠里，热胀冷缩使深色石头比浅色石头开裂得更快。
senses.why: Minerals expand at different rates, so a hot day and a cold night pull the grain boundaries apart.
senses.whyCN: 不同矿物膨胀速率不同，因此白天高温与夜间低温把颗粒边界拉开。

senses.title: Mechanical work by living things
senses.definition: roots prising joints open and animals digging or trampling rock and soil
senses.definitionCN: 根系把节理撑开，动物挖掘或踩踏岩石与土壤
senses.example: Root wedging counts as physical weathering even though a plant provides the force.
senses.exampleCN: 根劈作用虽由植物提供力量，仍算作物理风化。
senses.why: The category is defined by mechanism rather than by agent, so a root that acts like a wedge stays inside it.
senses.whyCN: 分类依据是机制而非施力者，因此像楔子一样起作用的根仍属此类。

senses.title: Damage to building stone
senses.definition: frost, salt and thermal cycling breaking the surface of masonry and monuments
senses.definitionCN: 冻融、盐析与温度循环破坏砌体与纪念碑的表面
senses.example: Physical weathering has crumbled the carved edge of the old fountain.
senses.exampleCN: 物理风化已经把老喷泉的雕花边缘蚀成碎屑。
senses.why: Conservation borrowed the geological term because city stone meets the same forces in a shorter cycle.
senses.whyCN: 文物保护借用了这个地质术语，因为城市石材在更短的周期里遭遇同样的力量。

intro.en: The phrase joins physical, from Greek physis nature through Latin physicalis, with weathering, the English noun built on Old English weder, weather.
intro.cn: 这个短语把 physical 与 weathering 结合：前者出自希腊 physis「自然」，经拉丁 physicalis 传入；后者是英语名词，建立在古英语 weder「天气」之上。

items.en: Physis meant nature, the way things grow and behave, and the adjective physikos described what belongs to the natural order.
items.cn: physis 意为自然、万物生长与运作的方式，形容词 physikos 描述属于自然秩序的事物。

items.en: Medieval Latin physicalis rendered the Greek adjective, and English physical arrived through French with the sense of the material world as opposed to the mind.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 physicalis 转写了这个希腊形容词，英语 physical 经法语传入，取得「物质世界、与精神相对」的含义。

items.en: Weder meant weather and storm; the verb weather meant to leave something exposed to wind, rain and frost.
items.cn: weder 意为天气与风暴；动词 weather 意为让某物暴露在风雨与霜冻之中。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology divided weathering into a mechanical kind and a chemical kind, and physical was chosen for the mechanical one.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学把风化分为机械与化学两类，机械一类便选用了 physical 这个词。

items.en: Engineering and conservation adopted the phrase in the twentieth century for concrete, masonry and monuments, without changing its meaning.
items.cn: 二十世纪，工程与文物保护把这短语用于混凝土、砌体与纪念碑，词义并未改变。

note.en: Group one holds the sibling weathering terms; group two holds processes that are often mistaken for weathering itself.
note.cn: 第一组是并列的风化术语；第二组是常被误当成风化本身的过程。

entries.definition: Breakdown by reaction, so the minerals are altered or removed rather than merely broken.
entries.definitionCN: 由反应造成的分解，矿物被改变或带走，而不只是被弄碎。

entries.definition: Weathering where plants, animals or microbes supply the force or the acid; it can be physical or chemical underneath.
entries.definitionCN: 由植物、动物或微生物提供力或酸的风化；底层机制可以是物理的或化学的。

entries.definition: The general decay of rock in place, of which the physical kind is one branch.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石在原地衰变的统称，物理一类是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: Relating to matter and force; on its own it says nothing about rock decay.
entries.definitionCN: 与物质和力有关的；单独使用时不涉及岩石衰变。

entries.definition: The removal and carrying away of loosened material; weathering produces the material, erosion moves it.
entries.definitionCN: 把松动的物质剥离并搬走；风化产生物质，侵蚀搬运物质。

entries.definition: Falling apart into small pieces; it describes the outcome rather than the geological category.
entries.definitionCN: 碎成小块；描述的是结果，而非地质学分类。

entries.definition: Wearing away by friction from moving sediment, ice or wind; it is one mechanism inside physical weathering.
entries.definitionCN: 被移动的泥沙、冰或风摩擦磨损；它是物理风化的机制之一。

entries.definition: Decay where the rock stays put; if the debris is carried away the process has become erosion.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石留在原地的衰变；一旦碎屑被搬走，该过程就变成侵蚀。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek nature word, real mechanisms and real textbook contrasts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「自然」词、真实机制与真实教科书对照。

normal.en: Physical means by force: the rock breaks, the minerals stay the same.
normal.cn: physical 指靠力气：石头碎了，矿物还是原来的矿物。

normal.en: The classic list is frost, salt, unloading, abrasion and heat.
normal.cn: 经典清单是冻融、盐析、卸荷、磨蚀与冷热。

normal.en: Weathering stays in place, erosion carries away: keep the pair together.
normal.cn: 风化留在原地，侵蚀负责搬运：把这对词一起记。

normal.en: Root wedging shows that the mechanism, not the agent, decides the category.
normal.cn: 根劈说明决定分类的是机制，而不是施力者。

normal.en: Physical evidence is the same mineral in smaller pieces.
normal.cn: 物理风化的证据就是同样的矿物变成了更小的块。

abstract.en: Picture water in a crack turning to ice and pushing like a slow jack.
abstract.cn: 想象裂缝里的水结成冰，像一只缓慢的千斤顶往外顶。

abstract.en: Picture a cliff peeling like the layers of an onion once the weight above is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象上方的重量消失后，崖壁像洋葱一样一层层剥开。

abstract.en: Picture wind carrying sand that sands down a stone pillar over a century.
abstract.cn: 想象风带着沙，用一百年把一根石柱磨细。

examples.en: Physical weathering prepares the rock for chemical attack by exposing fresh surfaces.
examples.cn: 物理风化通过暴露新鲜表面，为化学侵蚀做好准备。

examples.en: In polar regions physical weathering dominates because water keeps freezing.
examples.cn: 在极地，由于水反复结冰，物理风化占主导。

examples.en: The study measured physical weathering on exposed granite blocks.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了裸露花岗岩块上的物理风化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「物理 + 风化」——冻、盐、胀、磨，全用蛮力把石头拆开，成分一点没变

root: physical（希腊 physis「自然」加 -ikos，经拉丁 physicalis 与法语）+ weathering（古英语 weder「天气」加 -ing）；「以机械力把岩石弄碎而成分不变」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the umbrella process to five concrete mechanisms, then to plants acting as wedges and finally to the same damage seen on buildings.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从总过程走到五种具体机制，再到植物充当楔子，最后落到建筑上看到的同一类破坏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ice in a crack pushing a block loose.
core.cn: 核心意象：裂缝里的冰把石块顶松。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: force does the work and chemistry stays unchanged.
branches.cn: 类别：由力量做功，化学性质不变。

branches.en: GROWING THINGS IN PORES: ice and salt both push outward from inside.
branches.cn: 孔隙里的生长物：冰与盐都从内部向外顶。

branches.en: RELEASED PRESSURE: rock expands and sheets off once the load is gone.
branches.cn: 释放的压力：荷载消失后岩石膨胀并成片剥落。

branches.en: MOVEMENT AND HEAT: grinding by sediment and cracking by daily temperature swings.
branches.cn: 运动与热：泥沙的磨擦与日夜温差造成的开裂。

branches.en: OTHER AGENTS: roots act as wedges, and city stone suffers the same fate faster.
branches.cn: 其他施力者：根充当楔子，城市石材更快遭遇同样的命运。

intro.en: Physical weathering is readable as phys- plus -ical for the first word, and weather plus -ing for the second.
intro.cn: physical weathering 可拆读：前一词为 phys- 加 -ical，后一词为 weather 加 -ing。

latinIntro.en: The phys- stem is Greek, mediated by Latin physicalis; weather is native English. The Latin entries below record the mediating forms rather than an inherited Latin compound.
latinIntro.cn: phys- 词干来自希腊语，经拉丁 physicalis 中介；weather 是英语本族词。下面的拉丁词条记录的是中介形式，而不是拉丁语祖传复合词。

items.example: The stem appears in physics, physical and physician.
items.exampleCN: 该词干出现在 physics、physical 与 physician 中。

items.example: Physical and chemical are a standard pair.
items.exampleCN: physical 与 chemical 是标准的一对。

items.meaning: the science of matter and energy
items.meaningCN: 研究物质与能量的学科
items.example: Physics explains why ice expands when it freezes.
items.exampleCN: 物理学解释了冰结冰时为何膨胀。

items.example: The rock was physically broken, not dissolved.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石是被物理弄碎的，而不是被溶解的。

items.meaning: the state of the air; to expose to it
items.example: The stone weathered until its corners rounded.
items.exampleCN: 那块石头一直被风化，直到棱角变圆。

items.example: Weathering names the process, not the rubble.
items.exampleCN: weathering 命名的是过程，而不是碎屑。

items.example: Weathered granite feels rough under the hand.
items.exampleCN: 风化的花岗岩摸上去很粗糙。

items.meaning: the alternation of freezing and melting
items.exampleCN: 冻融循环驱动冰楔作用。

latinEntries.structure: Medieval Latin physicalis, from Greek physikos + Latin -alis
latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin physicalis is the adjective behind English physical.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 physicalis 是英语 physical 背后的形容词。

definition_zh: 学科；（大学的）学科门类；学术训练与规范
definition_en: a branch of knowledge with its own methods, standards and body of study, as established in universities
core_image: 走廊两侧每个办公室门口都挂着不同学科的名牌，学生抱着书从一扇门走向另一扇
scene: 走廊两侧每个办公室门口都挂着不同学科的名牌，学生抱着书从一扇门走向另一扇，墙上的公告列着各学科的评审规则。 Every academic discipline has its own way of judging evidence.
sceneCN: 这里指「学科」（第 1 个义项：拥有自身方法、标准与研究对象的学问门类）；句意为每一门学科都有自己判断证据的方式。图中可辨识物件：学科名牌、抱着书的学生、评审规则公告、走廊。

pos.zh: 学术训练；学术规范（不可数）
学科规训（知识体系对人的塑造，抽象）

senses.title: A branch of knowledge
senses.titleCN: 学科；有系统方法的学问门类
senses.definition: a field of study with its own subject matter, methods and standards
senses.definitionCN: 拥有自身研究对象、方法与标准的学问领域
senses.example: Every academic discipline has its own way of judging evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 每一门学科都有自己判断证据的方式。
senses.why: the two words combine a school's name with the idea of training, so a discipline is a field defined by how it trains its students.
senses.whyCN: 两个词把「学校」之名与「训练」之意合起来，因此学科是按「如何训练学生」来界定的一片领域。

senses.title: A university subject unit
senses.definition: an institutional unit in which that field is taught and examined
senses.definitionCN: 讲授并考核该领域的建制单位
senses.example: The committee reviews each academic discipline every five years.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会每五年评审每一个学科。
senses.why: a discipline is first a field of instruction, and the unit that teaches it took the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 学科原指一门教学领域，讲授它的建制单位便沿用了这一名称。

senses.title: Scholarly training
senses.definition: the training and standards that shape how work in a field is done
senses.definitionCN: 塑造某一领域工作方式的训练与标准
senses.example: The program teaches the discipline of careful citation.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目教授严谨引证这一学术规范。
senses.why: training is the older sense of the second word; a field without training is only a topic.
senses.whyCN: 「训练」是第二个词的旧义；没有训练的领域只是一个话题。

senses.title: The shaping of a learner
senses.titleCN: 学科规训（知识体系对人的塑造，抽象）
senses.definition: the way a field's rules gradually form the habits and judgement of its students
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域的规则逐步塑造学生习惯与判断力的方式
senses.example: Years of academic discipline changed how she read a page.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的学科规训改变了她读一页书的方式。
senses.why: training in a field imposes its rules on the learner, so the field's name came to mean that shaping.
senses.whyCN: 在某一领域受训就是把其规则加在学人身上，于是领域之名也指这种塑造。

senses.title: A research field within a discipline
senses.titleCN: 某一学科内的研究领域
senses.definition: a specialised area inside a larger field, with its own journals and questions
senses.definitionCN: 较大领域内更专门的分区，有自己的期刊与问题
senses.example: Medieval trade is a small discipline inside history.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪贸易是历史学内部的一个小研究领域。
senses.why: a bounded field of study inside a larger one is treated as a discipline of its own.
senses.whyCN: 较大领域内有边界的研究范围，被当作一门独立的学科。

senses.title: A hybrid branch
senses.definition: a field formed where two or more disciplines overlap
senses.definitionCN: 由两个或更多学科交叠而成的领域
senses.example: Bioinformatics grew as a new academic discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 生物信息学作为一门新学科成长起来。
senses.why: where two fields overlap, the overlap is organised and taught as a new discipline.
senses.whyCN: 两个领域重叠之处被组织起来，并作为新的学科来教授。

senses.title: The ethical code of scholarship
senses.titleCN: 学术纪律；学术共同体的行为规范
senses.definition: the shared rules of honesty, attribution and evidence that scholars enforce
senses.definitionCN: 学者共同维护的诚实、署名与证据规则
senses.example: Plagiarism violates the discipline of the profession.
senses.exampleCN: 抄袭违反这一行业的学术纪律。
senses.why: the field's rules of proof and attribution are enforced like a discipline imposed on its members.
senses.whyCN: 该领域关于论证与归属的规则，像加在成员身上的纪律那样被执行。

senses.title: Any field requiring long training
senses.titleCN: 比喻：需要长期训练才能掌握的专门领域
senses.definition: any specialised sphere that demands years of guided practice
senses.definitionCN: 任何需要多年有人指导的练习才能掌握的专门领域
senses.example: Restoring old violins is a discipline of the hands and ears.
senses.exampleCN: 修复古提琴是一门要靠手与耳朵的专门功夫。
senses.why: any body of practice with its own method was seen as a field one must be trained into.
senses.whyCN: 任何有自身方法的实践体系，都被看成必须经过训练才能进入的领域。

intro.en: The phrase joins academic, from the name of Plato's school, to discipline, from Latin disciplina 'instruction'.
intro.cn: 这个短语把来自柏拉图学园之名的 academic 与出自拉丁 disciplina「教导」的 discipline 连在一起。

items.en: Akadēmeia was the grove outside Athens where Plato taught, named after the hero Akademos.
items.cn: Akadēmeia 是雅典城外柏拉图讲学的那片园林，得名于英雄阿卡德摩斯。

items.en: English academic first meant 'of the school of Plato', then 'of universities and scholarship'.
items.cn: 英语 academic 先指「属于柏拉图学园的」，后指「属于大学与学问的」。

items.en: Discere meant 'to learn', the verb behind disciple as well as discipline.
items.cn: discere 意为「学习」，既是 disciple 的词源，也是 discipline 的词源。

items.en: Disciplina meant instruction and the training that goes with it, and later also a branch of study.
items.cn: disciplina 指教导及随之而来的训练，后来又指一门学问分支。

items.en: English discipline kept both faces, the training and the rule, and universities applied it to fields of study.
items.cn: 英语 discipline 两面都保留：训练与规则；大学又把它用到学科领域上。

items.en: Dating note: the date when the two words became a fixed phrase is approximate, and the extension from 'training' to 'field' is generally accepted but not precisely dated.
items.cn: 年代说明：两个词凝成固定短语的年代只是约数；从「训练」扩展到「学科」一般认为是自然引申，但年代不精确。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the learning and schooling roots; group two holds other names for areas of study.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「学习」与「学园」词根的词；第二组是其他指研究领域的名称。

entries.definition: An adjective for university life and scholarship; alone it names a person who works in higher education.
entries.definitionCN: 形容大学生活与学术的；单用时指在高校工作的人。

entries.definition: A learned society or specialised school; it keeps the place-name at the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 学者团体或专门学校；以地名为核心。

entries.tag: of rules or of a field
entries.definition: An adjective with two readings, one about punishment and one about the boundaries of a field.
entries.definitionCN: 有两个读法的形容词：一关于惩戒，一关于学科边界。

entries.definition: A person who insists on rules; it has nothing to do with fields of study.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持规则的人；与学科领域无关。

entries.definition: A school or university subject; broader and looser than a discipline, which implies method.
entries.definitionCN: 学校或大学里的科目；比学科更宽、更松，学科则含方法之意。

entries.definition: A general area of research or activity; it need not have a settled method.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指研究或活动的领域；不必然有定型的方法。

entries.definition: The subject a student specialises in; it describes a course of study, not a body of knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 学生主修的专业；指一段学习安排，而非知识体系。

entries.definition: A plain phrase for any organised subject; it carries no claim about method or standards.
entries.definitionCN: 对任何成体系科目的朴素说法；不对方法或标准作任何主张。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real campus plates and real review rules.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词根、真实学科名牌与真实评审规则。

normal.en: A school's name plus the word for training: a field defined by how it trains its students.
normal.cn: 「学园之名」加「训练」：按如何训练学生来界定的一片领域。

normal.en: The second word also means rule, which is why the phrase can cover academic conduct.
normal.cn: 第二个词也指规则，因此这个短语也能覆盖学术行为。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: academic discipline, interdisciplinary study, core discipline.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：学科、跨学科研究、核心学科。

normal.en: The learning root also gives disciple, one who learns.
normal.cn: 表示「学习」的词根还构成表示「门徒」的词，即学习的人。

normal.en: A discipline is more than a topic: it has methods and standards.
normal.cn: 学科不只是一个话题：它有方法与标准。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor where each door plate is a different way of asking questions.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每块门牌都是一种不同的提问方式。

abstract.en: Picture a garden with many paths, each worn by generations of feet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座园子有许多条路，每条都被一代代脚步磨出痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a hand taught to hold a tool in one exact way.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手被训练成以唯一正确的方式握工具。

examples.en: Every academic discipline has its own way of judging evidence.
examples.cn: 每一门学科都有自己判断证据的方式。

examples.en: Bioinformatics grew as a new academic discipline at the edge of biology and computing.
examples.cn: 生物信息学作为生物学与计算科学交界处的新学科成长起来。

examples.en: Years of academic discipline changed how she read a page.
examples.cn: 多年的学科规训改变了她读一页书的方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「学园」加「训练」：靠一套训练方法立起来的学问 → 学科

root: 短语由 academic 与 discipline 合成；academic 出自希腊 Akadēmeia「柏拉图讲学的园林」，discipline 出自拉丁 disciplina「教导」，其动词 discere 意为「学习」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses start from a field with methods, then its institutional unit, its training, its shaping of a learner, its specialised corners, its hybrid branches, its ethical rules and finally any field that demands long practice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「有方法的学问领域」开始，再是其建制单位、训练、对学习者的塑造、专门分区、交叉分支、伦理规则，最后是任何需要长期练习的领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor of door plates, each standing for one way of asking questions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条走廊上的一排门牌，每块代表一种提问方式。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS CORNERS: the whole discipline, then a specialised area inside it.
branches.cn: 领域与其角落：先是整门学科，再是它内部的一个专门分区。

branches.en: FORMS IN INSTITUTIONS: the standing unit, and the hybrid branch formed at the edges.
branches.cn: 建制中的形态：常设单位，以及边界处长出的交叉分支。

branches.en: TRAINING AND ITS EFFECT: the standards taught, then the habits they leave in a learner.
branches.cn: 训练与其效果：先是所教的标准，再是它们在学习者身上留下的习惯。

branches.en: THE RULE SIDE: honesty and attribution enforced by the field itself.
branches.cn: 规则一侧：由领域自身维护的诚实与署名规则。

branches.en: BORROWED CRAFT: any sphere that demands years of guided practice.
branches.cn: 借用的技艺：任何需要多年有人指导的练习的领域。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek place-name turned adjective to a Latin word for instruction; both halves still build their own families.
intro.cn: 这个短语把由希腊地名转成的形容词与拉丁「教导」一词连起来，两半各自仍构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek Akadēmeia gives academic and academy; Latin discere 'to learn' gives discipline, disciple and disciplinary.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 Akadēmeia 衍生出 academic 与 academy；拉丁 discere「学习」衍生出 discipline、disciple 与 disciplinary。

items.meaningCN: 柏拉图讲学的那片园林
items.example: The name of the grove became the name of schooling.
items.exampleCN: 园林之名后来成了学校之名。

items.meaning: of the school or of scholarship
items.example: The academic year begins in autumn.
The academy elected three new members.
items.exampleCN: 该学会选出了三位新成员。

items.example: The root supplies the learning behind the training.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供训练背后的「学习」。

items.example: The discipulus followed the master for years.
Disciplina covered both lesson and order.
items.exampleCN: 这个词同时覆盖课业与秩序。

items.meaning: training, rule, and later a field
items.example: The discipline has its own journals.

definition_zh: n. 服务员；看管人员；随从；adj. 伴随而来的；随之发生的
definition_en: A person whose job is to look after a place or serve customers; as an adjective, accompanying something as a result or circumstance.
core_image: 站在旁边随时准备接手的那个人
scene: 停车场的看管员在入口亭里抬手示意司机往前开。 The parking attendant lifted a hand to wave the driver forward.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attendant 指在某个场所负责看管或服务的人员。

senses.title: A person who serves or watches
senses.definition: someone employed to look after a place, help customers or keep order
senses.definitionCN: 受雇看管场所、帮助顾客或维持秩序的人
senses.example: The lift attendant checked every floor.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯服务员逐层检查。
senses.why: Attend once meant to wait upon someone, so the -ant ending names the person doing that waiting.
senses.whyCN: attend 早期意为「侍候某人」，因此加 -ant 就指做这种侍候工作的人。

senses.title: An accompanying result
senses.definition: as an adjective, going along with something as a natural consequence or circumstance
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指作为自然结果或情形伴随某事而来
senses.example: They discussed the surgery and its attendant risks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们讨论了手术及随之而来的风险。
senses.why: The person sense is one who stands beside; the adjective keeps only the standing beside, applied to abstract things.
senses.whyCN: 人的义项是「站在旁边的人」；形容词只保留「站在旁边」，用来修饰抽象事物。

senses.title: A follower in a retinue
senses.definition: in older or formal use, a companion or servant travelling with a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时或正式用法中，指随同显贵出行的同伴或仆从
senses.example: The bishop arrived with two attendants.
senses.exampleCN: 主教带着两名随从抵达。
senses.why: Court language kept the waiting sense alive as a noun for the people who formed the train of a great person.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷语言把「侍候」义保留下来，用来指组成显贵随行队伍的人。

intro.en: Attendant is attend plus -ant; attend comes from Old French atendre, to wait for, from Latin attendere, to stretch towards, from ad-, to, and tendere, to stretch.
intro.cn: attendant 是 attend 加 -ant；attend 来自古法语 atendre「等待」，出自拉丁语 attendere「朝向伸展」，由 ad-「向」与 tendere「伸展」构成。

items.en: The root ten- meant to stretch, the reaching of attention towards something.
items.cn: 词根 ten- 意为「伸展」，即注意力朝某物伸过去。

items.en: Latin tendere meant to stretch or direct, the source of tend and extend.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为「伸展、指向」，是 tend 与 extend 的来源。

items.en: With ad-, to, it became attendere, to stretch towards, hence to give heed.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」成为 attendere「朝……伸展」，进而指「留意」。

items.en: Old French atendre meant to wait for, which shifted stretch into waiting.
items.cn: 古法语 atendre 意为「等待」，把「伸展」转成了「等候」。

items.en: Middle English took the French present participle as attendaunt, one who waits upon another.
items.cn: 中古英语借入法语现在分词作 attendaunt，指侍候他人的人。

items.en: By the fifteenth century attendant named a servant and, later, anything accompanying.
items.cn: 到十五世纪 attendant 既指仆从，后来又指任何伴随之物。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the attend family and one other -ant noun; the near-meaning group lists people who serve and one adjective of accompaniment.
note.cn: 形近组保留 attend 词族和另一个 -ant 名词；近义组列出服务人员和表示伴随的形容词。

normalIntro.en: Attendant is attend plus -ant: the one who attends, or the thing that attends upon an event.
normalIntro.cn: attendant 是 attend 加 -ant：侍候的人，或伴随某事而来的东西。

normal.en: Flight attendant is the commonest job title.
normal.cn: flight attendant 是最常见的职业名称。

normal.en: The adjective sits before risks or problems.
normal.cn: 形容词用法常放在 risks 或 problems 之前。

normal.en: -ant names a person; -ance names the act.
normal.cn: -ant 指人，-ance 指行为。

normal.en: Attendance is the act, attendant is the person.
normal.cn: attendance 是行为，attendant 是人。

normal.en: Attendant circumstances is a set legal phrase.
normal.cn: attendant circumstances 是固定法律用语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：attend「侍候、照料」+ -ant「做……的人」——在旁边照料的人就是 attendant。

root: 拉丁语 tendere「伸展」加 ad-「向」成 attendere「把注意力伸向」，古法语 atendre 转为「等待、侍候」；加 -ant 指人，即 attendant，形容词保留「伴随」义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses keep the same picture of standing beside: a worker beside you, a result beside an event, a servant beside a lord.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都保留「站在旁边」这幅画面：身旁的服务员、事件旁的结果、显贵旁的随从。

intro.en: Attendant is at- plus tend plus -ant; the tend root also builds attend, extend, intend and tension.
intro.cn: attendant 是 at- 加 tend 加 -ant；tend 词根还构成 attend、extend、intend 与 tension。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is tendere, to stretch, attendere, to give heed, and tensio, a stretching; the -ant ending is the Latin present participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 tendere「伸展」、attendere「留意」与 tensio「张力」；-ant 词尾就是拉丁语现在分词。
